The same paper gave MOTS-c to mice at three ages — young, middle-aged and old — and found improved physical performance in all three groups. Treatment started late in life, three times a week, improved physical capacity and measures of healthspan.

This is where the phrase "exercise mimetic" entered the MOTS-c conversation, and it is worth handling carefully. The human half of that study showed MOTS-c is released by exercise. The mouse half showed that giving MOTS-c improves performance. Neither showed that injecting MOTS-c substitutes for training in a person. The most defensible reading is that MOTS-c is part of the machinery through which exercise produces its benefits — which, if anything, is an argument for training, not a replacement for it.

The One Human Trial

MOTS-c itself has never been through a published clinical trial. Its closest analog has, and the story is instructive.

A biotech company co-founded by the peptide's discoverer developed CB4211, a modified version of MOTS-c designed to have better drug-like properties than the natural peptide. It went into a Phase 1a/1b study for fatty liver disease and obesity — the first mitochondrial-derived peptide ever tested in humans.

The Phase 1a stage tested safety in 65 healthy adults. The Phase 1b stage was randomised, double-blind and placebo-controlled: twenty obese participants with at least 10% liver fat, given 25 mg by subcutaneous injection daily for four weeks. Topline results in August 2021 reported the drug was well tolerated with no serious adverse events, alongside significant reductions in the liver enzymes ALT and AST, a significant fall in glucose, and a trend toward lower body weight.

Those are encouraging exploratory findings in twenty people over four weeks. What happened next is the part usually left out. The company later stated that the formulation used in the Phase 1b stage was not suitable for further development, that efforts to produce an improved formulation had not succeeded, and that it was seeking a partner for the programme. In 2023 the company merged into an oncology business and the mitochondrial peptide pipeline was not carried forward. CB4211 has not advanced since.

One claim to be sceptical of

Several websites state that MOTS-c has completed a Phase 1 human safety study at doses up to 10 mg. That appears to be a garbled account of the CB4211 trial, which tested a different molecule at 25 mg. No published clinical trial has ever administered MOTS-c itself to humans, and no human pharmacokinetic data for it exists. If a source tells you otherwise, check what compound it is actually describing.

Dosing in the Research

Because no human trial of MOTS-c exists, there is no dose that has ever been validated in a person. What circulates instead is a convention, and it is worth seeing where that convention came from.

FuenteDosisRutaWhat it tells you
Original 2015 mouse workRoughly 0.5–15 mg/kg depending on the experimentIntraperitonealWhere the whole field starts; a route not used in people
2021 aged-mouse studyHigh mg/kg range, three times weeklyIntraperitonealThe origin of the 3×/week rhythm people use
CB4211 Phase 1b (an analog)25 mg once daily, 4 weeksSubcutáneoThe only human dosing data — for a different molecule
Community protocol convention5–10 mg per injection, 2–3× weeklySubcutáneoNot derived from any trial in humans or animals

Scaling animal doses to humans is done with a standard body-surface-area conversion, which for mouse to human divides by roughly twelve. Run it and the numbers are striking. A 5 mg/kg mouse dose scales to about 28 mg for a 70 kg adult. A 15 mg/kg mouse dose scales to about 85 mg. The 5–10 mg figure people actually use sits well below both.

Visual 2 · The Scaling Gap
What the animal doses scale to, versus what people actually inject.

Whether the common dose reflects sensible caution or is simply too low to do anything is not known. No study has compared them in people.

That gap is the honest headline for MOTS-c dosing. The schedule people follow was inherited from a mouse study; the amount was not. Neither has been tested in a human.

Efectos Secundarios y Seguridad

There is no clinical safety database for MOTS-c. The analog trial found its 25 mg dose well tolerated over four weeks in twenty people, with injection-site reactions the notable issue, and that is the entirety of the controlled human safety record for anything in this class.

What users report

Drawing on self-experimenter reports rather than trials, the commonly described effects are increased heart rate or palpitations, injection-site irritation, insomnia, and fever. None of this has been characterised systematically, and none of it should be read as a complete list.

Three situations that deserve specific caution

If you take metformin, insulin, or a sulfonylurea. MOTS-c works by activating AMPK — the same broad territory metformin operates in — and by increasing glucose uptake into muscle. Stacking it with glucose-lowering medication has never been studied and creates a plausible route to hypoglycaemia. This is the interaction most worth taking seriously. If you have a cardiac arrhythmia or structural heart disease. Palpitations and raised heart rate are among the most commonly reported effects, and AMPK activation affects how cardiac tissue handles energy. If you have or have had cancer. AMPK activation and antioxidant gene regulation both intersect with tumour biology in ways that cut in more than one direction, and the net effect has not been studied. No data exists for pregnancy or breastfeeding either.

Competitive athletes: read this twice

MOTS-c is named explicitly on the WADA Prohibited List. It appears under hormone and metabolic modulators, in the AMPK activator subcategory, alongside AICAR — spelled out in full as "mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c (MOTS-c)". It is prohibited at all times, in and out of competition.

This is not the usual situation where a research peptide gets swept up by a catch-all clause. WADA went to the trouble of naming this specific molecule. Several peptide sites state that MOTS-c is not on the list; they are wrong, and an athlete relying on that would be relying on a factual error. If you are subject to anti-doping testing, treat MOTS-c as a prohibited substance and confirm the current position with your national anti-doping organisation.

How MOTS-c Compares

MOTS-c gets grouped with several very different compounds. The distinctions are worth keeping straight.

CompuestoCómo funcionaHuman evidenceWADA status
MOTS-cAMPK activation via the folate cycle and AICARGenetic and observational only; no interventional trialNamed explicitly; prohibited at all times
AICARDirect AMP mimetic; activates AMPK directlyLarge cardiac surgery trials; never approvedNamed explicitly; prohibited since 2009
SLU-PP-332ERR agonist; endurance programme without AMPKRodent onlyNot named; treat as prohibited
GLP-1 drugsAppetite and gastric emptyingLarge phase 3 trials; approvedNot prohibited
SS-31Binds cardiolipin in the mitochondrial membranePhase 2/3 trials; mixed resultsNot named

The most important comparison is the one not in the table. If your goal is better insulin sensitivity, more mitochondria, and improved metabolic flexibility, resistance training plus zone-two cardio produces all three, has the strongest evidence base of anything on this page, and is the intervention that raises your own MOTS-c twelve-fold. Nothing here substitutes for that.

Where MOTS-c Stands Legally

MOTS-c is not approved as a finished pharmaceutical drug by the FDA, the EMA, or Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud. It is sold as a research compound. Two recent developments are worth knowing about.

  • 2023 — the FDA placed MOTS-c, along with a group of other peptides, in Category 2 of its 503A bulk drug substances list, blocking compounding pharmacies from preparing it.
  • April 2026 — the FDA removed twelve substances, MOTS-c among them, from Category 2 for further evaluation.
  • July 2026 — the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee reviewed seven peptides. MOTS-c was among the six recommended for the 503A Bulks List, on a narrow vote and over the objection of the FDA's own scientific reviewers.

It is easy to over-read that vote. It is advisory and non-binding; the FDA still has to run a separate rulemaking process that typically takes a year or more; and nothing about the compound's legal status has changed as a result. It is also not a statement that the evidence is strong — FDA staff had recommended against listing all seven, citing thin data. What the vote reflects is a policy shift toward access, not a new body of research.

None of this affects sport. A favourable compounding recommendation and a WADA prohibition are entirely separate systems, and the WADA position on MOTS-c has not moved. Our guide to research peptides versus pharmaceutical peptides explains what "research compound" means in practice for quality and oversight.

Preguntas frecuentes

Does MOTS-c actually work in humans?

Nobody knows, because it has never been tested. The animal data is strong and consistent, the human genetic data suggests the peptide matters in our physiology, and the analog trial produced encouraging four-week biomarker changes in twenty people. That is a reasonable basis for interest and not a basis for confidence.

Is MOTS-c a weight-loss peptide?

It is studied in a different way from the GLP-1 compounds. Those work substantially through appetite — you eat less, so you lose weight. In mice, MOTS-c reduced fat mass without reducing food intake, by shifting how fuel is used rather than how much is eaten. Whether that translates to meaningful weight change in a person is untested. If weight loss is the goal, see our guide on cómo funcionan los péptidos GLP-1 for the compounds that do have trial data.

Can I take MOTS-c with metformin or berberine?

This is the combination question that deserves a real answer rather than a shrug. Both metformin and MOTS-c push on AMPK signalling and glucose handling, and stacking two agents with overlapping effects on blood glucose without any study of the combination is how people end up hypoglycaemic. Anyone on glucose-lowering medication should be talking to the doctor who prescribed it before adding anything. See also our overview of interacciones de medicamentos peptídicos.

Will MOTS-c make me fail a drug test?

If you are tested under the WADA code, yes — that is the entire point of it being on the list by name. It is prohibited in and out of competition. Recreational lifters not subject to anti-doping rules are not affected by WADA, but anyone in a tested sport, including many amateur and masters competitions, should treat this as disqualifying.

Does MOTS-c replace cardio?

No, and the research points the other way. The human finding was that exercise produces MOTS-c — a roughly twelve-fold rise in muscle. The mouse findings suggest it may be one of the messengers exercise uses. The most sensible reading is that MOTS-c is downstream of training, so training is the thing with the evidence behind it.

¿Cuánto tiempo hasta que note algo?

There is no published human timeline, so any specific answer would be invented. In the analog trial, biomarker changes were measured at four weeks. Since the effects being studied are metabolic rather than sensory, there may be nothing to feel at all — which makes bloodwork more informative than subjective impressions if you are working with a clinician.

Should MOTS-c be cycled?

Cycling schedules for MOTS-c come from general peptide convention rather than from any receptor-downregulation data specific to this compound. The three-times-weekly rhythm most protocols use was inherited from a mouse study design, not from a finding about tolerance. It is fair to say the schedules are plausible; it is not fair to say they are evidence-based.

How is MOTS-c stored and reconstituted?

Sealed lyophilized vials keep frozen and protected from light; once reconstituted, the solution stays refrigerated at 2–8°C. MOTS-c dissolves readily in bacteriostatic water with no special solvent needed. Our guides on reconstitución y almacenamiento de péptidos en climas tropicales cover the practical side, which matters more here than in temperate countries.

What sizes does Peptides Costa Rica stock, and what does MOTS-c cost?

MOTS-c is listed in 10 mg and 40 mg vials. Current pricing and live stock are on the MOTS-C product page, and five or more vials of the same product carry an automatic 15% discount. Message us if you want a stock check before ordering.

Is MOTS-c legal in Costa Rica?

It is sold here as a research compound, the same framework used in most countries with an active peptide market, and is not approved as a finished pharmaceutical drug by the Ministerio de Salud, the FDA or the EMA. Our Preguntas frecuentes covers ordering and delivery within Costa Rica.

Questions about MOTS-c?

Happy to talk through what the research supports and what it doesn't — including whether this is the right compound for what you are trying to achieve, or whether something with more human data would serve you better.

Contáctenos por WhatsApp

Aviso importante: The information in this guide is general educational content only. It is not medical advice, a prescription, or a personalized recommendation. MOTS-c is not approved by the FDA, the EMA, or Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud as a finished pharmaceutical drug for human use, and is sold as a research compound intended for laboratory and scientific study. In July 2026 the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee recommended MOTS-c for inclusion on the 503A Bulks List; that recommendation is advisory, non-binding, and does not change the compound's legal status or make it an approved medicine. It is not a treatment for obesity, type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance, fatty liver disease, or any other condition. No clinical trial of MOTS-c in humans has been published and no human pharmacokinetic data exists; the efficacy evidence described here comes from rodent and cell studies, from human observational and genetic research, and from a four-week Phase 1b study of CB4211, a different molecule. Dosing ranges discussed reflect what is reported in published animal research and community use; they are not endorsements of those doses for any specific individual, and no dose has been validated in a person. MOTS-c activates AMPK and increases glucose uptake, creating a plausible risk of hypoglycaemia in combination with metformin, insulin, sulfonylureas or other glucose-lowering agents; no interaction studies exist. Reported effects include increased heart rate and palpitations. No safety data exists for pregnancy, breastfeeding, or long-term use, and the effect on tumour biology has not been studied. MOTS-c is named explicitly on the WADA Prohibited List under hormone and metabolic modulators and is prohibited at all times, in and out of competition. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before beginning any peptide protocol. Products sold by Peptides Costa Rica are intended for laboratory and research purposes only.

Fuentes
  1. Metabolismo celular (Lee y col., 2015): The discovery paper identifying MOTS-c within the mitochondrial 12S rRNA and describing folate-cycle inhibition, AICAR accumulation and AMPK activation in skeletal muscle.
  2. Nature Communications (Reynolds et al., 2021): Exercise induces MOTS-c in human skeletal muscle and circulation; MOTS-c treatment improved physical capacity in young, middle-aged and old mice.
  3. Aging (Zempo, Kim, Cohen et al., 2021): Meta-analysis of three cohorts totalling over 27,000 people linking the m.1382A>C variant and the K14Q form of MOTS-c to type 2 diabetes risk in men, with an interaction with physical activity.
  4. Journal of Clinical Investigation (Miller, Kim, Kumagai, Yen & Cohen, 2022): Review of mitochondrial-derived peptides in aging, including the decline of circulating MOTS-c with age and its inverse relationship with BMI and insulin resistance.
  5. Cell Metabolism (Kim et al., 2018): Demonstration that MOTS-c translocates to the nucleus under metabolic stress and regulates nuclear gene expression.
  6. CohBar, Inc. corporate disclosures and SEC filings (2021–2023): Phase 1a/1b topline results for the MOTS-c analog CB4211, and the subsequent statement that the formulation used was unsuitable for further development.
  7. ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03998514): Registration details for the CB4211 Phase 1a/1b study in obese participants with fatty liver disease.
  8. Agencia Mundial Antidopaje: Prohibited List, hormone and metabolic modulators, naming MOTS-c among prohibited AMPK activators.
  9. U.S. Anti-Doping Agency: Athlete guidance on AICAR and other prohibited AMPK activators, and on reported adverse effects of MOTS-c self-experimentation.
  10. Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EE. UU. 503A bulk drug substances list and the July 2026 Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee proceedings.

Longevity & Anti-Aging

NAD+ Injections: What to Know

NAD+ has become one of the most talked-about molecules in longevity — and injections are the most effective way to use it at home. Here's what it does, how to use it, and what to realistically expect.

NAD+ Injections at a Glance
What It Is
A coenzyme found in every cell
Main Interest
Cellular energy & longevity
Typical Dose
50–150 mg per injection
How It's Given
Subcutaneous injection
Our Vial
500 mg lyophilized
Known For
A brief sting at the injection site
What's on this page
  1. What NAD+ Actually Is
  2. Why NAD+ Declines With Age
  3. Why Inject Instead of Taking a Pill
  4. What It's Studied For
  5. Dosing & How to Use It
  6. The Sting: What to Expect
  7. Side Effects & Safety
  8. Injection vs IV Drip
  9. What to Realistically Expect
  10. Common Questions
  11. Sources

If you've spent any time reading about longevity, you've come across NAD+. It's one of the most researched molecules in the entire field, and for good reason — it sits at the center of how your cells make energy and repair themselves. The catch is that NAD+ levels fall as you age, and the body doesn't absorb it well when you simply swallow it. That's where injections come in.

This guide covers what NAD+ is, why people inject it, what the research actually supports, and the practical details of using it — including the one thing everyone asks about: the brief sting some people feel during the injection.

What NAD+ Actually Is

NAD+ stands for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide — but the name matters less than what it does. Think of NAD+ as a worker that every cell in your body relies on. It's a coenzyme, which means it helps your cells carry out essential chemical reactions. Without enough of it, those reactions slow down.

NAD+ has two main jobs that make it interesting for health and aging:

Making Energy

NAD+ is essential to how your mitochondria — the tiny power plants inside your cells — turn food into usable energy. Less NAD+ means less efficient energy production.

Repair & Maintenance

NAD+ powers proteins called sirtuins (sometimes called "longevity genes") and helps repair damaged DNA. These are central to how cells stay healthy over time.

One quick point of honesty: NAD+ is technically a coenzyme, not a peptide. But it's so central to the longevity conversation, and so often used alongside peptides, that it's almost always grouped with them. We carry it for the same audience that's interested in our other longevity compounds.

Why NAD+ Declines With Age

Here's the finding that put NAD+ on the map for longevity research: your NAD+ levels drop substantially as you get older. By middle age, many people have a fraction of the NAD+ they had in their youth.

This decline isn't just a number on a chart. Lower NAD+ has been linked to several things we associate with aging — reduced cellular energy, less efficient DNA repair, declining mitochondrial function, and slower cellular maintenance. Because NAD+ touches so many systems at once, researchers consider its age-related decline one of the more fundamental drivers of how the body ages. In fact, NAD+ is connected to several of the recognized "hallmarks of aging," which is why it shows up in so many longevity discussions.

The natural question that follows is: if NAD+ drops with age and matters this much, can restoring it help? That's exactly what the research interest is built around — and why people use injections to raise their levels.

Why Inject Instead of Taking a Pill

You may have seen NAD+ sold as pills or capsules, often as "precursors" like NMN or NR (ingredients your body converts into NAD+). So why bother with injections?

The answer comes down to absorption. When you swallow NAD+ itself, very little of it survives your digestive system and makes it into your bloodstream intact. Your gut breaks it down before it can be used. Oral precursors like NMN and NR work around this by giving your body the raw materials to make NAD+ rather than NAD+ itself, but this is an indirect route that relies on several conversion steps.

Injecting NAD+ skips the digestive system entirely. A subcutaneous injection (into the fatty layer just under the skin) delivers NAD+ directly where it can be absorbed into your bloodstream — far more efficiently than a pill. For people who want a direct, reliable way to raise their NAD+ levels, injection is the most effective at-home option.

The short version

Pills containing NAD+ mostly get broken down before they can work. Precursor pills (NMN/NR) take an indirect path. Injections deliver NAD+ directly into your system, which is why they're the preferred route for people serious about raising their levels. Our broader piece on why injections beat pills explains the absorption science in more detail.

What NAD+ Is Studied For

NAD+ is researched across a wide range of areas. Here's an honest summary of where the interest lies — keeping in mind that much of the strongest evidence comes from laboratory and animal studies, with human research still developing.

Energy & Fatigue

Because NAD+ is central to energy production, it's widely studied and used for combating low energy and fatigue. Many users report improved energy as one of the first things they notice.

Cellular Aging

Through its effects on sirtuins and DNA repair, NAD+ is one of the most studied molecules in longevity research — a cornerstone of many anti-aging protocols.

Mental Clarity & Focus

NAD+ plays a role in brain energy metabolism, and improved focus and mental clarity are commonly reported, often within the first few sessions.

Metabolic Health

NAD+ is involved in how cells process energy and nutrients, making it a subject of interest for metabolic function and healthy aging.

Mood & Stress

NAD+ is involved in the metabolism of brain chemicals like serotonin and dopamine, and some users report improvements in mood and a calmer baseline.

Recovery & Sleep

Better sleep quality is a frequently reported effect, often emerging in the second or third week of consistent use.

It's worth being clear: while the biology behind NAD+ is well understood and increasingly validated, NAD+ has not been proven to extend human lifespan, and it's not an approved treatment for any specific condition. The research is genuinely promising, but realistic expectations matter — more on that below.

Dosing & How to Use It

NAD+ injections use a "start low, go slow" approach more than almost any other compound — mostly because of the sting and flushing that higher doses can cause (covered in the next section). Starting small lets your body adjust comfortably.

Parameter Common Range
Starting dose 25–50 mg (to assess your tolerance)
Typical dose 50–150 mg per injection, often around 100 mg
Frequency Several times per week (often 3–7x)
Route Subcutaneous (just under the skin)
Best timing Earlier in the day — NAD+ can be energizing and may disrupt sleep if taken late

Reconstituting Your 500 mg Vial

Our NAD+ comes as a 500 mg freeze-dried vial. A common way to prepare it is to mix it with 5 ml of bacteriostatic water, which gives you a concentration of 100 mg per ml. At that strength:

  • A 50 mg dose = 50 units on a standard insulin syringe (half an ml)
  • A 100 mg dose = 100 units (a full ml)

For step-by-step mixing and injection instructions, our how to reconstitute peptides and dosing and injection basics guides walk through the whole process. Use a standard insulin syringe (29–31 gauge), the same kind used for most subcutaneous injections.

The golden rule with NAD+: go slow

More than the dose itself, the speed of your injection matters with NAD+. Injecting slowly is the single most effective way to minimize the sting and flushing. Start with a low dose, inject it slowly over several seconds, and increase only once you know how your body responds. Patience here makes the whole experience much more comfortable.

The Sting: What to Expect

This is the thing NAD+ is famous for, so let's address it directly. Unlike most peptides — which you barely feel going in — NAD+ injections can produce a brief stinging or burning sensation at the injection site, and sometimes a flushing feeling (warmth, redness in the face or chest). It surprises people who weren't expecting it, so knowing about it in advance makes a big difference.

Why It Happens

There are two reasons. First, NAD+ in solution tends to be acidic, which can cause a stinging sensation under the skin. Second, NAD+ activates the same receptor responsible for the well-known "niacin flush" (the warm, tingly feeling some people get from high-dose vitamin B3), which causes blood vessels to widen and produces that flushing sensation.

The Good News

None of this is dangerous, and it's very manageable. Here's how to keep it minimal:

1

Inject slowly

This is the most important tip by far. Pushing the plunger slowly over several seconds dramatically reduces both the sting and the flushing. Rushing is what makes it uncomfortable.

2

Start with a low dose

Smaller doses cause less sensation. Beginning at 25–50 mg lets your body get used to NAD+ before you work up to a larger dose.

3

It fades with time

Most people find the sting and flushing become milder as their body acclimates over the first several injections. What feels noticeable at first often becomes barely noticeable later.

The brief sting usually lasts only a few minutes, and any flushing typically passes within an hour. For most people, once they know what to expect and inject slowly, it's a minor and temporary trade-off.

Side Effects & Safety

Beyond the injection-site sting and flushing, NAD+ is generally well tolerated. The most commonly reported effects are mild and short-lived.

  • Injection site stinging or burning — the most common, lasting a few minutes (minimized by injecting slowly)
  • Flushing — warmth or redness, especially at higher doses, usually passing within an hour
  • Mild nausea — occasional, more likely with larger doses or fast injection
  • Headache or short-term fatigue — infrequent, usually during the early adjustment period
  • Trouble sleeping — if taken too late in the day, since NAD+ can be energizing (take it earlier to avoid this)

Who Should Be Cautious

  • Pregnant or breastfeeding women (no safety data)
  • People with existing liver or kidney conditions — these organs process NAD+, so medical guidance is important
  • Anyone taking prescription medications, who should check with a healthcare professional first
  • People with a history of cancer, as a general precaution applied across peptide and longevity compounds

⚠ A note on storage

Like all peptides, NAD+ must be stored properly. Keep the dry powder cold, and once mixed, keep it refrigerated and use it within a few weeks — never freeze the mixed solution. In a tropical climate this matters even more; see our guide to storing peptides in tropical climates for the full details.

Injection vs IV Drip

You may have heard of NAD+ IV drips offered at wellness clinics, which can cost hundreds of dollars per session. Here's how they compare to at-home subcutaneous injections.

Subcutaneous Injection IV Drip
Where At home, yourself At a clinic, with supervision
Absorption Gradual, steady Immediate, high peak
Cost Much lower per dose Often hundreds per session
Convenience High — fits any schedule Requires appointments
Comfort Brief sting, passes quickly Flushing/nausea during drip if too fast

IV drips deliver a large amount quickly and produce a high peak in your bloodstream, but they're expensive, require clinic visits, and the fast delivery can actually cause more intense flushing and nausea during the infusion. Subcutaneous injections deliver a steadier, gentler dose at a fraction of the cost, and you can do them on your own schedule. For ongoing, maintenance-style use, most people find injections the more practical choice.

What to Realistically Expect

Honest expectations make for a much better experience, so here's the straight version.

The Timeline Varies

Some people notice more energy and mental clarity within the first few sessions. For others, the benefits build more gradually over several weeks as cellular NAD+ stores are replenished. Sleep and mood improvements often show up around the second or third week. There's natural variation — don't judge it by your first injection.

It's a Foundation, Not a Miracle

NAD+ is best thought of as supporting your cellular energy and maintenance systems, not as a dramatic overnight transformation. The most common realistic benefits people describe are better energy, sharper focus, improved sleep, and a general sense of vitality. Anyone promising it will turn back the clock is overselling.

Consistency Matters

NAD+ works through replenishing levels over time, so regular, consistent use produces better results than occasional injections. It rewards a steady routine.

The Basics Still Come First

NAD+ works best alongside the fundamentals that support healthy aging — good sleep, regular exercise, solid nutrition, and stress management. Interestingly, exercise itself naturally boosts NAD+, so the two work in the same direction. NAD+ supplements your healthy habits; it doesn't replace them.

Common Questions

Does the NAD+ injection really sting?

It can, yes — this is the one thing NAD+ is known for. The sting comes from NAD+ being mildly acidic, and some people also feel a warm flushing sensation. The good news is it's harmless, usually lasts only a few minutes, and is easy to minimize: inject slowly, start with a low dose, and it tends to fade as your body adjusts over the first several injections. Most people find it a minor, temporary trade-off.

How do I reduce the stinging?

Injecting slowly is by far the most effective method — push the plunger gently over several seconds rather than quickly. Starting at a lower dose (25–50 mg) also helps, as does giving your body time to acclimate over the first few sessions. Together, these steps make the experience much more comfortable.

Why not just take NAD+ pills?

When you swallow NAD+, most of it gets broken down in your digestive system before it can reach your bloodstream. Pills containing precursors like NMN or NR take an indirect route — giving your body materials to make NAD+ rather than NAD+ itself. Injections deliver NAD+ directly into your system, bypassing the gut, which is why they're the most effective at-home option for raising your levels.

When should I inject NAD+?

Earlier in the day is best. NAD+ tends to be energizing, so injecting it late in the evening can interfere with sleep for some people. Morning or early afternoon is the common choice, letting you benefit from any energy boost during the day.

How quickly will I notice anything?

It varies. Some people report more energy and mental clarity within the first few sessions; others notice changes building gradually over several weeks. Sleep and mood improvements often emerge around the second or third week. NAD+ works by replenishing your levels over time, so consistency produces better results than occasional use.

Is injection better than an IV drip?

For most people doing ongoing maintenance, yes. IV drips deliver a fast, high peak but cost hundreds per session, require clinic visits, and the rapid delivery can cause more intense flushing and nausea. Subcutaneous injections give a steadier dose at a fraction of the cost, on your own schedule. IV has its place for high-dose loading under supervision, but injections are the practical choice for regular use.

Can I combine NAD+ with other peptides?

Yes — NAD+ is often considered a foundational part of longevity protocols and pairs well with other compounds that target different aging pathways. It's commonly combined with growth hormone peptides, mitochondrial peptides like MOTS-c, and others. As always, if you're new to peptides, establish how NAD+ affects you on its own before adding anything else. Our best anti-aging peptides guide covers how the longevity compounds fit together.

Is NAD+ safe?

NAD+ is generally well tolerated, with side effects that are usually mild and short-lived — mainly the injection-site sting, occasional flushing, and sometimes mild nausea at higher doses. Because your liver and kidneys process NAD+, people with conditions affecting those organs should get medical guidance first, as should anyone pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking prescription medications. Our are peptides safe guide covers the broader safety picture.

Is NAD+ legal in Costa Rica?

NAD+ is sold as a research compound in Costa Rica, the same framework used in most countries with active peptide markets. It is not approved as a finished pharmaceutical drug by the Costa Rica Ministerio de Salud, FDA, or EMA, and is sold for laboratory and research purposes. Buying locally avoids the heat exposure that international shipping puts peptides through. See our FAQ page for more.

Thinking about trying NAD+?

If you have questions about NAD+, the injection process, or whether it fits your goals, just reach out. We answer every message personally — no pressure, no upsell.

Si has pasado tiempo leyendo sobre longevidad, te habrás topado con el NAD+. Es una de las moléculas más investigadas en todo el campo, y por una buena razón: se encuentra en el centro de cómo tus células producen energía y se reparan. El inconveniente es que los niveles de NAD+ disminuyen con la edad, y el cuerpo no lo absorbe bien cuando simplemente se ingiere. Ahí es donde entran las inyecciones.

Esta guía cubre qué es el NAD+, por qué la gente se lo inyecta, qué respaldan realmente las investigaciones y los detalles prácticos de su uso, incluido aquello sobre lo que todos preguntan: el breve escozor que algunas personas sienten durante la inyección.

Qué es realmente el NAD+

NAD+ significa dinucleótido de nicotinamida y adenina, pero el nombre importa menos que lo que hace. Piensa en el NAD+ como un trabajador del que dependen todas las células de tu cuerpo. Es una coenzima, lo que significa que ayuda a tus células a llevar a cabo reacciones químicas esenciales. Sin suficiente cantidad, esas reacciones se ralentizan.

El NAD+ tiene dos funciones principales que lo hacen interesante para la salud y el envejecimiento:

Generación de energía

El NAD+ es esencial para que tus mitocondrias —las diminutas centrales eléctricas dentro de tus células— conviertan los alimentos en energía utilizable. Menos NAD+ significa una producción de energía menos eficiente.

Reparación y mantenimiento

El NAD+ alimenta a unas proteínas llamadas sirtuinas (a veces denominadas "genes de la longevidad") y ayuda a reparar el ADN dañado. Estos son fundamentales para que las células se mantengan sanas con el tiempo.

Un punto rápido de honestidad: NAD+ es técnicamente una coenzima, no un péptido. Pero es tan central en la conversación sobre longevidad y se usa tan a menudo junto con péptidos, que casi siempre se agrupa con ellos. Lo ofrecemos para el mismo público interesado en nuestros otros compuestos de longevidad.

Por qué el NAD+ disminuye con la edad

Aquí está el hallazgo que puso al NAD+ en el mapa para la investigación de la longevidad: tus niveles de NAD+ disminuyen sustancialmente a medida que envejeces. A la mediana edad, muchas personas tienen una fracción del NAD+ que tenían en su juventud.

Esta disminución no es solo un número en una gráfica. Los niveles bajos de NAD+ se han relacionado con varias cosas que asociamos con el envejecimiento: menor energía celular, reparación del ADN menos eficiente, disminución de la función mitocondrial y un mantenimiento celular más lento. Dado que el NAD+ afecta a tantos sistemas a la vez, los investigadores consideran que su declive relacionado con la edad es uno de los impulsores más fundamentales de cómo envejece el cuerpo. De hecho, el NAD+ está conectado con varias de las "señales del envejecimiento" reconocidas, razón por la cual aparece en tantas discusiones sobre longevidad.

La pregunta natural que se sigue es: si el NAD+ disminuye con la edad y es tan importante, ¿puede su restauración ayudar? Eso es exactamente lo que rodea el interés en la investigación, y por lo que las personas usan inyecciones para aumentar sus niveles.

¿Por qué inyectarse en lugar de tomar una pastilla?

Es posible que hayas visto el NAD+ vendido en píldoras o cápsulas, a menudo como "precursores" como NMN o NR (ingredientes que tu cuerpo convierte en NAD+). Entonces, ¿por qué molestarse con las inyecciones?

La respuesta se reduce a la absorción. Cuando ingieres NAD+ por sí solo, muy poco de él sobrevive a tu sistema digestivo y llega a tu torrente sanguíneo intacto. Tu intestino lo descompone antes de que pueda ser utilizado. Los precursores orales como el NMN y el NR sortean esto al darle a tu cuerpo las materias primas para producir NAD+ en lugar de NAD+ en sí, pero esta es una ruta indirecta que depende de varios pasos de conversión.

La inyección de NAD+ evita por completo el sistema digestivo. Una inyección subcutánea (en la capa grasa justo debajo de la piel) administra el NAD+ directamente donde puede ser absorbido por el torrente sanguíneo, de manera mucho más eficiente que una pastilla. Para las personas que buscan una forma directa y confiable de aumentar sus niveles de NAD+, la inyección es la opción más efectiva para usar en casa.

La versión corta

Las píldoras que contienen NAD+ en su mayoría se descomponen antes de que puedan funcionar. Las píldoras precursoras (NMN/NR) toman un camino indirecto. Las inyecciones entregan NAD+ directamente a tu sistema, por eso son la vía preferida para las personas serias en cuanto a elevar sus niveles. Nuestro artículo más amplio sobre por qué las inyecciones son mejores que las pastillas La ciencia de la absorción, en un sentido más profundo, se refiere al estudio de cómo una sustancia (el absorbente) toma y retiene otra sustancia (la sustancia absorbida o el absorbato). Este proceso es fundamental en innumerables aplicaciones científicas y tecnológicas, y su comprensión detallada implica varios aspectos clave: 1. **Mecanismos de Absorción:** Existen diferentes mecanismos que explican cómo ocurre la absorción: * **Absorción Física (Fisisorción):** En este tipo, las fuerzas entre el absorbente y el absorbato son débiles, principalmente fuerzas de Van der Waals. Es un proceso reversible y generalmente ocurre a bajas temperaturas. La cantidad de sustancia absorbida depende de la presión (o concentración) y la temperatura. Los ejemplos incluyen la adsorción de gases en superficies sólidas o la disolución de un gas en un líquido. * **Absorción Química (Quimisorción):** Aquí, se forman enlaces químicos fuertes (covalentes o iónicos) entre el absorbente y el absorbato. Este proceso es a menudo irreversible o requiere una cantidad significativa de energía para revertirse. La quimisorción es más específica y depende de la reactividad química de las especies involucradas. Ejemplos incluyen la catálisis heterogénea, donde los reactivos se adsorben químicamente en la superficie de un catalizador. * **Absorción en Masa (Bulk Absorption):** A diferencia de la adsorción que ocurre principalmente en la superficie, la absorción en masa implica la penetración de la sustancia absorbida *dentro* del volumen del material absorbente. Esto ocurre comúnmente con líquidos absorbiendo gases o sólidos absorbiendo líquidos o gases. Un ejemplo clásico es la absorción de dióxido de carbono en hidróxido de sodio líquido. 2. **Termodinámica de la Absorción:** * **Entalpía de Absorción:** Representa el cambio de energía cuando ocurre la absorción. La fisisorción tiene una entalpía de absorción baja y negativa (exotérmica), mientras que la quimisorción tiene una entalpía de absorción más alta y negativa. * **Entropía de Absorción:** El proceso de absorción generalmente resulta en una disminución de la entropía, ya que las moléculas del absorbato se vuelven más ordenadas al unirse al absorbente. * **Energía Libre de Gibbs:** La espontaneidad de la absorción se describe mediante la energía libre de Gibbs (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS). Si ΔG es negativa, el proceso es espontáneo. 3. **Cinética de la Absorción:** Se refiere a la velocidad a la que ocurre la absorción. Factores como el área superficial del absorbente, la concentración del absorbato, la temperatura y la presencia de barreras de difusión influyen en la cinética. 4. **Isotermas de Absorción:** Estas curvas describen la relación entre la cantidad de sustancia absorbida y la concentración (o presión) del absorbato a una temperatura constante. Existen varios modelos de isotermas, como: * **Isotermas de Langmuir:** Asumen la formación de una monocapa en sitios de absorción específicos y homogéneos. * **Isotermas de Freundlich:** Describen la absorción en superficies heterogéneas y no necesariamente forman una monocapa. * **Isotermas de BET (Brunauer-Emmett-Teller):** Amplían la teoría de Langmuir para incluir la formación de multicapas, útil para caracterizar el área superficial de materiales porosos. 5. **Factores que Afectan la Absorción:** * **Naturaleza del Absorbente:** La composición química, la estructura física (porosidad, área superficial, rugosidad) y las propiedades electrónicas del absorbente son cruciales. * **Naturaleza del Absorbato:** La polaridad, el tamaño molecular, la reactividad y la presión de vapor del absorbato juegan un papel importante. * **Temperatura:** Generalmente, la absorción disminuye con el aumento de la temperatura (especialmente la fisisorción), ya que la energía térmica puede superar las fuerzas de unión. * **Presión/Concentración:** A mayor presión o concentración del absorbato, mayor será la cantidad absorbida, hasta alcanzar un punto de saturación. * **Presencia de Otros Componentes:** Compuestos en la fase del absorbato pueden competir por los sitios de absorción, o pueden modificar las propiedades del absorbente. 6. **Aplicaciones de la Ciencia de la Absorción:** * **Purificación y Separación:** Absorción de gases contaminantes del aire o aguas residuales, separación de mezclas de gases (ej. separación de O2 y N2 en plantas de separación de aire), cromatografía. * **Almacenamiento de Gases:** Absorción de hidrógeno para almacenamiento de energía. * **Catálisis:** La catálisis heterogénea se basa fundamentalmente en la adsorción de reactivos en la superficie catalítica. * **Medicina:** Absorción de fármacos en el cuerpo humano, sistemas de liberación controlada. * **Ciencia de Materiales:** Desarrollo de nuevos materiales adsorbentes con alta capacidad y selectividad. * **Procesos Industriales:** Secado, deshumidificación, eliminación de impurezas. En resumen, la ciencia de la absorción es un campo multidisciplinario que abarca la física, la química y la ingeniería, centrándose en los principios subyacentes, los mecanismos, la termodinámica, la cinética y los factores que influyen en la interacción entre dos fases, con el objetivo de optimizar y utilizar estos procesos para diversas aplicaciones.

Para qué se estudia el NAD+

El NAD+ se investiga en una amplia gama de áreas. Aquí tienes un resumen honesto de dónde reside el interés, teniendo en cuenta que gran parte de la evidencia más sólida proviene de estudios de laboratorio y en animales, mientras que la investigación en humanos aún se está desarrollando.

Energía y fatiga

Dado que el NAD+ es fundamental para la producción de energía, es ampliamente estudiado y utilizado para combatir la falta de energía y la fatiga. Muchos usuarios reportan una mejora en sus niveles de energía como una de las primeras cosas que notan.

Envejecimiento celular

Gracias a sus efectos en las sirtuinas y la reparación del ADN, el NAD+ es una de las moléculas más estudiadas en la investigación sobre la longevidad, un pilar de muchos protocolos antienvejecimiento.

Claridad Mental y Enfoque

El NAD+ desempeña un papel en el metabolismo energético del cerebro, y a menudo se reportan mejora en el enfoque y la claridad mental, frecuentemente dentro de las primeras sesiones.

Salud metabólica

El NAD+ participa en cómo las células procesan la energía y los nutrientes, lo que lo convierte en un tema de interés para la función metabólica y el envejecimiento saludable.

Ánimo y estrés

El NAD+ participa en el metabolismo de químicos cerebrales como la serotonina y la dopamina, y algunos usuarios reportan mejoras en el estado de ánimo y una línea de base más calmada.

Recuperación y Sueño

Una mejor calidad del sueño es un efecto reportado frecuentemente, que a menudo aparece en la segunda o tercera semana de uso constante.

Vale la pena ser claros: aunque la biología detrás del NAD+ está bien entendida y cada vez más validada, no se ha demostrado que el NAD+ extienda la vida humana, ni es un tratamiento aprobado para ninguna condición específica. La investigación es realmente prometedora, pero las expectativas realistas importan, y profundizaremos en eso a continuación.

Dosificación y cómo usarlo

Las inyecciones de NAD+ utilizan un enfoque de "empezar bajo, ir lento" más que casi cualquier otro compuesto, principalmente debido al ardor y el enrojecimiento que las dosis más altas pueden causar (se abordará en la siguiente sección). Empezar con dosis bajas permite que tu cuerpo se ajuste cómodamente.

Parámetro Rango Común
Dosis inicial 25–50 mg (para evaluar tu tolerancia)
Dosis típica 50–150 mg por inyección, frecuentemente alrededor de 100 mg
Frecuencia Varias veces por semana (a menudo 3–7 veces)
Ruta Subcutáneo (justo debajo de la piel)
El mejor momento Más temprano en el día, el NAD+ puede ser energizante y puede interrumpir el sueño si se toma tarde.

Reconstitución de su vial de 500 mg

Nuestro NAD+ viene en presentación de 500 mg vial liofilizado. Una forma común de prepararlo es mezclarlo con 5 ml de agua bacteriostática, lo que le da una concentración de 100 mg por ml. A esa concentración:

  • Una dosis de 50 mg = 50 unidades en una jeringa de insulina estándar (medio ml)
  • Una dosis de 100 mg = 100 unidades (1 ml completo)

Para instrucciones de mezcla e inyección paso a paso, nuestro Cómo reconstituir péptidos y dosificación e inyección básicos Las guías te acompañan durante todo el proceso. Usa una jeringa de insulina estándar (calibre 29-31), el mismo tipo que se usa para la mayoría de las inyecciones subcutáneas.

La regla de oro con NAD+: ve despacio

Más que la dosis en sí, la velocidad La inyección de tu inyección con NAD+ es importante. Inyectar lentamente es la forma más efectiva de minimizar el escozor y el enrojecimiento. Comienza con una dosis baja, inyéctala lentamente durante varios segundos y aumenta solo una vez que sepas cómo responde tu cuerpo. La paciencia aquí hace que toda la experiencia sea mucho más cómoda.

El Golpe: Qué Esperar

Esta es la razón por la que el NAD+ es famoso, así que abordémoslo directamente. A diferencia de la mayoría de los péptidos, que apenas se sienten al aplicarse, las inyecciones de NAD+ pueden producir una sensación breve de picazón o ardor en el sitio de la inyección, y a veces una sensación de enrojecimiento (calor, rojez en la cara o el pecho). Esto sorprende a las personas que no lo esperaban, por lo que saberlo de antemano marca una gran diferencia.

Por qué sucede

Hay dos razones. Primero, el NAD+ en solución tiende a ser ácido, lo que puede causar una sensación de picazón o ardor bajo la piel. Segundo, el NAD+ activa el mismo receptor responsable del conocido "enrojecimiento por niacina" (la sensación cálida y de hormigueo que algunas personas experimentan con altas dosis de vitamina B3), que provoca la dilatación de los vasos sanguíneos y produce esa sensación de rubor.

Las Buenas Noticias

Nada de esto es peligroso y es muy manejable. Aquí te explico cómo mantenerlo al mínimo:

1

Inyectar lentamente

Este es, de lejos, el consejo más importante. Presionar el émbolo lentamente durante varios segundos reduce drásticamente tanto el pinchazo como la rojez. Apresurarse es lo que lo hace incómodo.

2

Empieza con una dosis baja

Dosis más bajas causan menos sensación. Comenzar con 25-50 mg permite que tu cuerpo se acostumbre al NAD+ antes de aumentar la dosis.

3

Se desvanece con el tiempo

La mayoría de las personas encuentran que el escozor y el enrojecimiento se vuelven más leves a medida que su cuerpo se acostumbra durante las primeras inyecciones. Lo que al principio se nota, a menudo se vuelve apenas perceptible después.

La breve picazón suele durar solo unos minutos, y cualquier enrojecimiento desaparece típicamente en una hora. Para la mayoría de las personas, una vez que saben qué esperar y se inyectan lentamente, es una compensación menor y temporal.

Efectos Secundarios y Seguridad

Más allá del escozor y el enrojecimiento en el sitio de la inyección, el NAD+ generalmente se tolera bien. Los efectos reportados con mayor frecuencia son leves y de corta duración.

  • Picazón o ardor en el sitio de la inyección — el más común, que dura unos minutos (minimizados al inyectar lentamente)
  • Desagüe — enrojecimiento o calor, especialmente en dosis más altas, que suele desaparecer en una hora
  • Náuseas leves — ocasional, más probable con dosis más altas o inyección rápida
  • Dolor de cabeza o fatiga a corto plazo — infrecuente, usualmente durante el período inicial de ajuste
  • Problemas para dormir — si se toma muy tarde en el día, ya que el NAD+ puede ser energizante (tómalo más temprano para evitar esto)

¿Quién debería tener precaución?

  • Mujeres embarazadas o en período de lactancia (no hay datos de seguridad)
  • Las personas con afecciones hepáticas o renales preexistentes —estos órganos procesan el NAD+, por lo que la guía médica es importante
  • Cualquier persona que tome medicamentos recetados, ¿con quién debe consultar primero a un profesional de la salud?
  • Las personas con antecedentes de cáncer, como una precaución general aplicable a compuestos de péptidos y longevidad

⚠ Una nota sobre el almacenamiento

Como todos los péptidos, el NAD+ debe almacenarse correctamente. Mantenga el polvo seco en frío y, una vez mezclado, guárdelo en el refrigerador y úselo dentro de unas pocas semanas; nunca congele la solución mezclada. En un clima tropical, esto cobra aún más importancia; consulte nuestro Guía para almacenar péptidos en climas tropicales para más detalles.

Inyección vs. Goteo IV

Es posible que hayas oído hablar de las infusiones intravenosas de NAD+ que se ofrecen en clínicas de bienestar, las cuales pueden costar cientos de dólares por sesión. Aquí comparamos cómo se comparan con las inyecciones subcutáneas en casa.

Inyección subcutánea Suero intravenoso
Dónde En casa, tú En una clínica, con supervisión
Absorción Gradual, constante Pico alto e inmediato
Costo Mucho menor por dosis A menudo cientos por sesión
Conveniencia Alto — se adapta a cualquier horario Requiere citas
Comodidad Picadura breve, pasa rápido Sofoco/náuseas durante la infusión si es demasiado rápida

Las infusiones intravenosas (IV) administran una dosis grande rápidamente y producen un pico alto en el torrente sanguíneo, pero son caras, requieren visitas a la clínica y la administración rápida puede causar un enrojecimiento y náuseas más intensos durante la infusión. Las inyecciones subcutáneas administran una dosis más constante y suave a una fracción del costo, y puedes aplicártelas según tu propio horario. Para un uso continuo, de mantenimiento, la mayoría de las personas encuentran que las inyecciones son la opción más práctica.

Qué esperar de forma realista

Las expectativas honestas hacen que la experiencia sea mucho mejor, así que aquí tienes la versión directa.

El cronograma varía

Algunas personas notan más energía y claridad mental en las primeras sesiones. Para otras, los beneficios se acumulan de forma más gradual durante varias semanas a medida que se reponen las reservas celulares de NAD+. Las mejoras en el sueño y el estado de ánimo a menudo aparecen alrededor de la segunda o tercera semana. Existe una variación natural; no juzgues los resultados por tu primera inyección.

Es una base, no un milagro

El NAD+ se entiende mejor como un apoyo a tus sistemas de energía celular y mantenimiento, no como una transformación drástica de la noche a la mañana. Los beneficios realistas más comunes que la gente describe son mayor energía, mayor concentración, mejor sueño y una sensación general de vitalidad. Cualquiera que prometa que revertirá el tiempo está exagerando.

La consistencia importa

El NAD+ funciona reponiendo los niveles con el tiempo, por lo que un uso regular y constante produce mejores resultados que las inyecciones ocasionales. Recompensa una rutina constante.

Lo básico sigue siendo lo primero

El NAD+ funciona mejor junto con los fundamentos que apoyan el envejecimiento saludable: buen sueño, ejercicio regular, nutrición sólida y manejo del estrés. Curiosamente, el ejercicio en sí mismo aumenta naturalmente el NAD+, por lo que ambos trabajan en la misma dirección. El NAD+ complementa tus hábitos saludables; no los reemplaza.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿La inyección de NAD+ realmente pica?

Sí, puede. Esto es lo único por lo que se conoce el NAD+. El escozor se debe a que el NAD+ es ligeramente ácido, y algunas personas también sienten una sensación de calor y enrojecimiento. La buena noticia es que es inofensivo, generalmente dura solo unos minutos y es fácil de minimizar: inyectar lentamente, comenzar con una dosis baja y tiende a desvanecerse a medida que su cuerpo se adapta durante las primeras inyecciones. La mayoría de las personas lo consideran un inconveniente menor y temporal.

¿Cómo reduzco la picazón?

La inyección lenta es, de lejos, el método más eficaz: presiona el émbolo suavemente durante varios segundos en lugar de hacerlo rápidamente. Comenzar con una dosis más baja (25-50 mg) también ayuda, al igual que darle tiempo a tu cuerpo para que se aclimate durante las primeras sesiones. Juntos, estos pasos hacen que la experiencia sea mucho más cómoda.

¿Por qué no simplemente tomar pastillas de NAD+?

Cuando ingieres NAD+, la mayor parte se descompone en tu sistema digestivo antes de que pueda llegar a tu torrente sanguíneo. Las pastillas que contienen precursores como NMN o NR toman una ruta indirecta: le dan a tu cuerpo materiales para producir NAD+ en lugar de NAD+ en sí. Las inyecciones entregan NAD+ directamente a tu sistema, evitando el intestino, por lo que son la opción casera más efectiva para elevar tus niveles.

¿Cuándo debo inyectarme NAD+?

Temprano en el día es lo mejor. El NAD+ tiende a ser energizante, por lo que inyectarlo al final de la noche puede interferir con el sueño de algunas personas. Por la mañana o a primera hora de la tarde es la opción común, lo que le permite beneficiarse de cualquier impulso de energía durante el día.

¿Qué tan rápido notaré algo?

Varía. Algunas personas reportan más energía y claridad mental dentro de las primeras sesiones; otras notan cambios que se manifiestan gradualmente a lo largo de varias semanas. Las mejoras en el sueño y el estado de ánimo suelen aparecer alrededor de la segunda o tercera semana. El NAD+ funciona reponiendo tus niveles con el tiempo, por lo que la constancia produce mejores resultados que el uso ocasional.

¿Es la inyección mejor que una vía intravenosa?

Para la mayoría de las personas que realizan mantenimiento continuo, sí. Las infusiones intravenosas (IV) entregan una dosis alta y rápida, pero cuestan cientos por sesión, requieren visitas a la clínica y la entrega rápida puede causar más enrojecimiento y náuseas intensos. Las inyecciones subcutáneas dan una dosis más estable a una fracción del costo, en tu propio horario. La IV tiene su lugar para dosis de carga altas bajo supervisión, pero las inyecciones son la opción práctica para uso regular.

¿Puedo combinar NAD+ con otros péptidos?

Sí, el NAD+ a menudo se considera una parte fundamental de los protocolos de longevidad y combina bien con otros compuestos que se dirigen a diferentes vías de envejecimiento. Se combina comúnmente con péptidos de hormona de crecimiento, péptidos mitocondriales como MOTS-c y otros. Como siempre, si eres nuevo en los péptidos, establece cómo te afecta el NAD+ por sí solo antes de agregar cualquier otra cosa. Nuestro los mejores péptidos antienvejecimiento La guía cubre cómo encajan los compuestos de longevidad.

¿Es seguro el NAD+?

content.html_en:
Foundations

Natural vs Synthetic Peptides

The distinction matters far less than the marketing suggests, and in a completely different way than most people expect. Here is what actually separates one peptide from another — and why "natural" has historically been the more dangerous option.

This guide covers peptide chemistry, manufacturing methods and the documented safety history of extracted versus synthesised peptide products. It is educational only and not a substitute for advice from a qualified healthcare professional. Sources are listed at the end.

What's on this page
  1. The Quick Answer
  2. What the Words Actually Mean
  3. Same Sequence, Same Molecule
  4. How Peptides Are Actually Made
  5. When "Natural" Went Badly Wrong
  6. Peptides That Aren't Natural at All
  7. Collagen: The Genuinely Natural Category
  8. What to Judge Instead
  9. Common Questions
  10. Sources

Search for peptides and you will eventually meet a page promising something "natural" as opposed to something "synthetic," with the implication running in the obvious direction. It is one of the more misleading framings in this field, and unpicking it turns out to be genuinely useful — not because the distinction is meaningless, but because the part that matters is not the part being sold.

Two things are true at once. Almost every peptide you can buy, including the ones described as natural, is made in a laboratory. And the small number of peptides that genuinely are extracted from living tissue have a documented safety record that is very much worse.

The Quick Answer

If you read nothing else

A peptide with a given amino acid sequence is the same molecule regardless of how it was made. Your body has no mechanism for detecting provenance. What differs between products is not "natural versus synthetic" but three other things: whether the sequence matches a human one or has been deliberately engineered, what impurities the manufacturing route leaves behind, and whether the batch in front of you was made properly. The last of those is the one you can actually check.

What the Words Actually Mean

Part of the confusion is that "natural" is doing at least four different jobs in peptide marketing, and they get conflated constantly.

"The sequence occurs in nature"

The most common meaning. The molecule matches something your body makes — but the product itself was still synthesised in a lab. This describes most of the catalogue.

"Extracted from a living source"

Genuinely derived from tissue, glands or animal material. Rare in modern peptides, and historically the source of the field's worst safety failures.

"Made by living cells"

Recombinant production — bacteria or yeast engineered to produce the peptide. Technically biological, technically manufactured. Neither camp cleanly.

"Not a drug"

A vibe rather than a fact. Used to imply gentleness or safety, with no chemical or regulatory meaning whatsoever.

"Synthetic," meanwhile, usually just means the peptide was assembled chemically rather than harvested. It says nothing about whether the resulting molecule is foreign to the body. Synthesised human insulin is chemically human insulin.

Same Sequence, Same Molecule

Here is the piece of chemistry that resolves most of the argument. A peptide is defined by its sequence of amino acids and the way that chain folds. Assemble those amino acids in that order and you have that peptide. There is no residual signature of the assembly process, no molecular fingerprint identifying where it came from.

Your receptors bind shapes. A receptor presented with the correct sequence responds to it, and there is no additional check on origin — no mechanism by which a cell could distinguish an identical molecule made three different ways. This is not a controversial position; it is the basis on which recombinant insulin replaced animal insulin worldwide.

Visual 1 · Three Routes, One Molecule
The manufacturing method changes what else is in the vial — not what the peptide is.

The peptide is the same. Everything else in the vial is not.

How Peptides Are Actually Made

Four routes account for essentially everything on the market, and each leaves a characteristic signature.

MethodHow it worksWhat it leaves behind
Solid-phase synthesisThe chain is built one amino acid at a time on an insoluble resin bead, then cleaved off. The dominant method for short peptides.Truncated and deletion sequences where a coupling step failed, plus residual solvents and trifluoroacetate from the cleavage step
Recombinant productionThe gene is inserted into bacteria or yeast, which produce the peptide as a living factory. Used for longer chains and proteins.Host cell proteins, DNA fragments and endotoxins that purification has to remove
ExtractionHarvested from animal or human tissue. Now almost entirely historical for peptides.Whatever else was in the source material, including pathogens
Enzymatic hydrolysisA large protein is broken into fragments with enzymes. This is how collagen peptides are made.A mixture of fragment sizes rather than a single defined molecule

Solid-phase synthesis deserves a moment, because it is how nearly everything in a research-peptide catalogue is produced. The method was developed by Bruce Merrifield, who won the 1984 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for it, and the principle is elegant: anchor the first amino acid to a bead, add the next, wash away everything that did not react, repeat. Because the growing chain stays fixed to the bead, excess reagents can be flushed away at every step.

The catch is that each coupling step is efficient but not perfect. Across thirty steps, small failures accumulate into a population of chains missing a residue here or there. This is precisely why purity testing exists, and why a purity figure on a certificate of analysis is a real number describing a real problem rather than marketing decoration.

When "Natural" Went Badly Wrong

The strongest argument against the natural-is-safer instinct is not theoretical. It is two well-documented episodes in twentieth-century medicine.

Growth hormone from cadaver pituitaries

Before recombinant production existed, human growth hormone could only be obtained one way: extracted from the pituitary glands of cadavers. In the United States, roughly 7,700 patients — mostly children being treated for growth failure — received it through a national programme between 1963 and 1985.

In 1985 the first cases appeared of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a fatal degenerative prion disease, in former recipients. Production stopped immediately. But prion diseases have incubation periods measured in decades — reported latencies have ranged from about 5 to 42 years — so cases continued to emerge long afterwards. As of early 2024, 254 cases worldwide had been linked to cadaver-derived growth hormone, including 36 among recipients of the US programme. More recently, researchers have also reported evidence of transmitted Alzheimer's pathology in some recipients.

The replacement was the synthetic version

Recombinant human growth hormone — somatropin, produced by inserting the human gene into E. coli — became commercially available in 1985 and is identical to the natural hormone, all 191 amino acids of it. It does not transmit prion disease, because it was never inside anyone. Hundreds of thousands of children have been treated with it since. The synthetic molecule is the same as the natural one; the manufacturing route was the entire difference between safe and fatal. For more on this compound family, see our guide on peptides versus HGH and our article on somatropin.

Insulin from slaughterhouses

The same pattern, with lower stakes and higher volume. For sixty years, insulin was extracted from cow and pig pancreases. Animal insulin works — porcine insulin differs from human by a single amino acid, bovine by three — but the impurities carried over from the extraction process were associated with allergic reactions, fat loss at injection sites, abscesses and antibody formation.

In October 1982 the FDA approved Humulin, recombinant human insulin produced in bacteria. It was the first drug of any kind made by recombinant DNA technology, and it substantially eliminated the allergy and impurity problems of the animal-derived product. Nobody has argued for a return to the natural version.

Even BPC-157 tells this story

The compound is described everywhere as derived from a protein in gastric juice, which is true as far as it goes. What is less often mentioned is why nobody extracts it. A patent covering its manufacture states the reasoning plainly: obtaining the natural protein from gastric juice was complex, the raw material source was uncertain, and there was a risk of viral contamination — so the fragment was chemically synthesised instead. Every unit of BPC-157 in circulation is made this way.

Peptides That Aren't Natural at All

Now the distinction that actually deserves your attention. Some peptides are exact copies of human sequences. Others are deliberately engineered molecules that no organism has ever produced — and those behave meaningfully differently from their natural counterparts.

Semaglutide is the clearest example. It is often described as a GLP-1 analogue, which undersells how much has been changed. Native GLP-1 survives about two minutes in the bloodstream before an enzyme chops it up. Semaglutide carries three modifications: a substituted amino acid at position 8 that the enzyme cannot cleave, a swap at position 34, and a fatty diacid chain attached at position 26 that binds tightly to albumin. Together these take the half-life from roughly two minutes to about a week. Two of those changes involve chemistry that does not exist in human biology at all.

Visual 2 · The Spectrum That Matters
Not natural versus synthetic — human sequence versus deliberately engineered.

Position on this spectrum tells you more about a compound than any "natural" label.

This matters because engineering is generally the point. A modification that stops an enzyme degrading a molecule is what makes weekly dosing possible instead of hourly. The trade-off is that a molecule your body has never encountered has effects your body has never had to handle, and those need to be established by trial rather than assumed from the natural version's safety record. See our guides on semaglutide and CJC-1295 for what that looks like compound by compound.

Collagen: The Genuinely Natural Category

One group of products genuinely is animal-derived, and it belongs in a different conversation entirely.

Collagen peptides are made by taking collagen from bovine hide, fish skin or similar sources and breaking it into fragments with enzymes. The result is not a single defined molecule but a mixture of short chains of varying length. They are eaten rather than injected, regulated as food rather than as drugs, and they do not act on a receptor the way the compounds discussed above do — they are digested and the amino acids reused.

So when someone contrasts "natural collagen peptides" with "synthetic peptides," they are comparing a food supplement with an injectable research compound. Both are called peptides; almost nothing else about them is comparable. Our guides on types of collagen peptides and our collagen peptides range cover that category properly.

What to Judge Instead

If provenance is the wrong question, here is the right one. Four things determine whether a peptide product is what it claims to be, and none of them appear on a label that says "natural."

Identity

Is it the molecule on the label? Mass spectrometry answers this. Wrong-compound and under-dosed products are a documented problem in this market.

Purity

What percentage is the intended peptide, and what is the rest? Usually measured by HPLC. The remainder is mostly truncated chains from imperfect synthesis.

Endotoxin

Bacterial fragments that cause fever and inflammation. Not covered by a standard purity assay — it needs a separate test that many certificates omit.

Provenance of the batch

Does the certificate name this batch, the testing laboratory and the date? A certificate that could belong to any lot is not evidence about yours.

That is the practical substitute for the natural-versus-synthetic question, and it is answerable. Our guide on understanding peptide purity and COAs explains how to read the documentation, and our COA database holds the results for what we carry.

One separate distinction is worth keeping straight, because it is frequently confused with this one: research-grade versus pharmaceutical-grade is a question about regulatory oversight and manufacturing standards, not about chemistry or origin. Our guide on research peptides versus pharmaceutical peptides covers that axis.

Common Questions

Are natural peptides safer than synthetic ones?

On the historical record, the opposite. The two peptide products genuinely extracted from biological tissue at scale — cadaver-derived growth hormone and animal insulin — both caused harm that synthetic and recombinant replacements eliminated. In one case that harm was fatal. Extraction carries contamination risk that chemical assembly does not.

Can my body tell the difference?

Not between identical molecules, no. Receptors respond to structure, and there is no additional origin check. Your body can absolutely tell the difference between a natural sequence and an engineered analogue — but that is a difference in the molecule itself, not in how it was made.

Is every peptide sold as a research compound synthetic?

Essentially all of the short ones, yes — made by solid-phase synthesis. Longer chains and true proteins, growth hormone being the obvious case, are generally produced recombinantly in bacteria or yeast. A product sold as extracted from tissue would be highly unusual and would warrant hard questions about its sourcing.

What does "bio-identical" mean here?

Borrowed from hormone marketing, where it means a molecule structurally identical to the human one regardless of manufacture. Applied honestly to a peptide it just means the sequence matches. It carries no implication about purity, potency or whether the product is any good, and it is not a regulatory term.

Do synthetic peptides leave chemical residues?

Some, which is exactly why purification matters. Solid-phase synthesis uses trifluoroacetic acid to cleave the finished chain from the resin, and trace trifluoroacetate can carry through as a counter-ion unless a salt exchange is performed. Solvent residues are also possible. These are known, testable, controllable issues — which is more than can be said for whatever was in a pituitary gland.

Is a higher purity percentage always better?

Broadly yes, with two caveats. Purity is only meaningful alongside identity — 99% pure of the wrong molecule is not reassuring. And a purity figure says nothing about endotoxin, which is tested separately and is arguably the more clinically relevant contaminant for anything injected.

Are plant-derived peptides a real thing?

Plants make peptides, and plant protein hydrolysates are used in food and cosmetics. But the compounds discussed in the peptide-therapy conversation are human or human-derived sequences, and a plant cannot supply those. A "plant-based" version of a human peptide would either be the same sequence produced recombinantly in a plant system, or it would not be that peptide.

Why is BPC-157 called natural if it's synthetic?

Because its sequence was reported as part of a larger protein found in gastric juice, so the description has some basis. Two caveats are worth knowing. The 15-amino-acid fragment does not circulate freely in the body — it is a laboratory construction. And subsequent researchers have noted that the sequence does not appear in the human genome, while the full parent protein sequence was never published, which leaves the natural derivation less settled than the marketing implies.

Does any of this affect what I should buy?

Only in the sense that it should redirect your attention. A vendor emphasising that a product is natural is telling you something with no chemical content. A vendor showing you batch-specific identity and purity testing is telling you something you can verify. Ask for the second.

Is any of this regulated in Costa Rica?

The compounds discussed here are sold as research compounds and are not approved as finished pharmaceutical drugs by Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud, the FDA or the EMA. There is no regulatory definition of "natural" applied to peptides in any of those jurisdictions, which is part of why the term is used so freely. Our FAQ page covers how ordering works locally.

Want to see the testing on what you're buying?

Ask us for the certificate of analysis on any batch — identity, purity, and where it was tested. We would rather you judge a product on its documentation than on a label. No pressure attached.

Contact Us on WhatsApp

Important disclaimer: The information in this guide is general educational content only. It is not medical advice, a prescription, or a personalized recommendation. Of the compounds named on this page, recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin), human insulin and semaglutide hold regulatory approval for specific medical indications; BPC-157, TB-500, sermorelin and CJC-1295 are not approved by the FDA, the EMA, or Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud as finished pharmaceutical drugs for human use and are sold as research compounds intended for laboratory and scientific study. Nothing on this page should be read as suggesting that a compound is safe or effective because of how it is manufactured; manufacturing method and clinical evidence are separate questions, and most research compounds have limited or no human trial data regardless of how they are produced. "Natural," "bio-identical" and similar terms have no regulatory definition when applied to peptides and should not be relied on as indicators of quality, purity or safety. The historical safety events described — Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease transmission through cadaver-derived growth hormone, and adverse reactions to animal-derived insulin — are drawn from the published record and are included to illustrate manufacturing risk, not to characterise any product currently on the market. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before beginning any peptide protocol. Products sold by Peptides Costa Rica are intended for laboratory and research purposes only.

  3. Nature Medicine (Banerjee et al., 2024): Report of iatrogenic Alzheimer's disease pathology in recipients of cadaveric pituitary-derived growth hormone.
  4. Clinical trial protocol documentation on recombinant human growth hormone: Recombinant somatropin produced in E. coli became commercially available in 1985 and is identical to the natural 191-amino-acid hormone.
  5. Reference pharmacology literature on animal-derived insulin: Impurities from extraction were associated with insulin allergy, lipoatrophy, abscesses and antibody formation; recombinant human insulin was developed to address these.
  6. Smithsonian Institution and FDA regulatory history: Humulin, licensed October 1982, was the first pharmaceutical of any kind produced by recombinant DNA technology.
  7. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1984 (Bruce Merrifield): Development of solid-phase peptide synthesis, and the role of trifluoroacetic acid in cleaving the completed chain from the resin.
  8. Peptide synthesis technical literature: Raw cleavage products contain truncated and deletion sequences plus reagent residues, requiring chromatographic purification and mass-spectrometric confirmation of identity.
