Metabolic & Weight

Semaglutide: The Complete Guide

The GLP-1 peptide that reshaped weight loss — known as Ozempic and Wegovy. Here's how it works, what the clinical trials actually showed, and what to know before considering it.

This guide summarizes published clinical research on semaglutide. It is educational only and not a substitute for advice from a qualified healthcare professional. Sources are listed at the end.

Semaglutide at a Glance
Class
GLP-1 receptor agonist
Brand Names
Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus
Trial Weight Loss
~15% of body weight (68 wks)
Dosing
Once weekly, titrated up
Half-Life
~7 days (weekly dosing)
Main Side Effects
Gastrointestinal, usually transient
What's on this page
  1. What Semaglutide Is
  2. The Names Explained
  3. How It Works
  4. What the Trials Showed
  5. Dosing & Titration
  6. Side Effects & Managing Them
  7. The Muscle-Loss Consideration
  8. How It Compares
  9. Safety & Who Should Avoid It
  10. Common Questions
  11. Sources

Few compounds have changed a field the way semaglutide changed weight management. When its landmark trial data was published, it showed something previously thought possible only through surgery: substantial, sustained weight loss from a weekly injection. It became a household name almost overnight — under the brands Ozempic and Wegovy — and reshaped how medicine approaches obesity.

This guide explains what semaglutide is, how it produces its effects, exactly what the clinical trials demonstrated, how it's dosed, and the practical realities of side effects and considerations — all grounded in the published research.

What Semaglutide Is

Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist — a peptide that mimics a natural gut hormone called glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). Your body releases GLP-1 after you eat; it helps regulate blood sugar and signals fullness. The catch is that natural GLP-1 breaks down within minutes. Semaglutide is engineered to resist that breakdown, so a single injection keeps working for about a week — which is why it's dosed just once weekly.

It was originally developed for type 2 diabetes (GLP-1 helps control blood sugar), but researchers noticed a consistent, striking side effect: significant weight loss. That observation led to dedicated obesity trials and, ultimately, to semaglutide becoming the defining weight-loss medication of its era.

The Names Explained (Ozempic vs Wegovy vs Rybelsus)

One source of confusion is that the same molecule — semaglutide — is sold under different brand names for different uses. Here's the plain breakdown:

Brand Primary Use Form
Ozempic Type 2 diabetes (used off-label for weight) Weekly injection, up to 2 mg
Wegovy Weight management (obesity) Weekly injection, up to 2.4 mg
Rybelsus Type 2 diabetes Daily oral tablet

They're all semaglutide — the differences are the approved use, the dose, and the form. The weight-loss trial results most people cite come from the higher 2.4 mg dose (Wegovy). As of 2026, an oral tablet form of semaglutide for weight loss has also been approved, expanding the options beyond injection.

How It Works

Semaglutide produces weight loss through several complementary actions — it's not a stimulant or a "fat burner," but a hormone signal that changes how much you want to eat.

Reduces Appetite

It acts on appetite centers in the brain, reducing hunger and cravings. Most people simply feel satisfied with less food — the central mechanism behind the weight loss.

Slows Gastric Emptying

It slows how quickly the stomach empties, so you feel full longer after eating. This is also the source of most of its digestive side effects.

Improves Blood Sugar Control

It prompts insulin release when blood sugar is high and reduces excess glucose output — the original diabetes mechanism.

Quiets "Food Noise"

Many users describe a reduction in constant intrusive thoughts about food, making it easier to eat less without white-knuckle willpower.

The key insight

Semaglutide works largely by reducing appetite — it makes eating less feel natural rather than forced. That "food noise" reduction is what many people find most striking: the constant background pull toward food quiets down. This is why it succeeds where willpower-based dieting often fails — it addresses the biological drive to eat, not just the behavior.

What the Trials Showed

Semaglutide's reputation rests on an unusually strong body of clinical trial evidence — the STEP program (Semaglutide Treatment Effect in People with obesity).

The Landmark Result

In the pivotal STEP 1 trial (published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021), 1,961 adults with obesity or overweight — without diabetes — received either weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo, alongside lifestyle support. After 68 weeks, the semaglutide group lost an average of about 14.9% of their body weight, compared to roughly 2.4% with placebo. For a non-surgical treatment, reaching close to 15% average weight loss was a genuine turning point — a level previously thought achievable only through bariatric surgery.

It Lasts

The STEP 5 trial extended the picture to two years, showing that the weight loss was sustained with continued treatment — this isn't just a short-term effect that quickly rebounds while you stay on it. Across the STEP program, results were consistent, and beyond weight, semaglutide has also shown cardiovascular benefits in separate research.

An honest note on stopping

One important, well-documented finding: much of the weight tends to return after stopping semaglutide, because the appetite-regulating effect ends when the medication does. This has reframed how the compound is understood — as an ongoing tool for managing a chronic condition (like blood pressure medication) rather than a short course that permanently "fixes" weight. It's worth going in with that realistic understanding.

Dosing & Titration

Semaglutide dosing follows one firm principle: start low and increase slowly. This gradual titration is the single most important factor in tolerating it well. The ranges below reflect the standard approach used in trials and labeling. They are general informational references, not medical recommendations.

Phase Typical Weekly Dose Purpose
Weeks 1–4 0.25 mg Adaptation — not expected to drive weight loss yet
Weeks 5–8 0.5 mg Continued adaptation
Weeks 9–12 1.0 mg Building toward an effective dose
Weeks 13–16 1.7 mg Approaching target
Week 17+ 2.4 mg (target) The full weight-management dose from the trials

Why you can't rush this

The 0.25 mg starting dose is about tolerability, not effectiveness — you shouldn't expect much weight loss at the lowest doses, and that's by design. Skipping steps or escalating too fast is the single most common cause of severe, intolerable nausea and of people quitting altogether. Your digestive system needs time to adapt to slowed gastric emptying. Patience through the titration is what makes the difference between tolerating it well and having a miserable experience. Some people also stay at a lower dose that works for them rather than always pushing to the maximum.

Semaglutide comes as a solution or is reconstituted from powder with bacteriostatic water, then injected subcutaneously once weekly. See our reconstitution and dosing basics guides, and our tropical storage guide for keeping it stable in the heat.

Side Effects & Managing Them

Semaglutide's side effects are predictable and mostly digestive — a direct consequence of how it slows the gut. The good news is they're usually most intense early on and fade as your body adjusts, and there's a lot you can do to minimize them.

Common (usually transient)

  • Nausea — the most common, especially early and after dose increases
  • Constipation or diarrhea
  • Reduced appetite (the intended effect, but worth eating enough nutrition)
  • Bloating, burping, or reflux
  • Fatigue, particularly early on

Practical ways to reduce them

  • Eat smaller portions — slowed emptying means large meals feel worse
  • Favor bland, lower-fat foods when nausea is present; go easy on greasy and very rich meals
  • Stay hydrated, which also helps with constipation
  • Don't rush the dose titration — this is the biggest lever
  • Eat enough protein and stay active (see the muscle note below)

When to seek medical attention

Contact a healthcare professional if you can't keep food or water down, or if you experience severe or persistent abdominal pain (especially pain radiating to the back, which can signal pancreatitis — a rare but serious concern). Rapid weight loss can also raise the risk of gallstones. These are uncommon, but they're the situations where medical input matters. See our when to consult a doctor guide.

The Muscle-Loss Consideration

One increasingly discussed aspect of GLP-1 weight loss deserves honest attention: some of the weight lost is lean muscle, not just fat. Research suggests that roughly 25–40% of the weight lost on GLP-1 medications can come from lean mass. This isn't unique to semaglutide — significant weight loss from any cause involves some muscle loss — but it's worth actively countering.

How to protect your muscle

Two countermeasures matter most: eat enough protein (this becomes harder when your appetite is suppressed, so it needs to be deliberate) and do resistance training (lifting weights or bodyweight work signals your body to preserve muscle). Losing weight while keeping muscle gives a better body composition and metabolic outcome than just watching the scale drop. This is important enough that we cover it — and how growth-hormone peptides sometimes factor in — as part of a broader metabolic strategy.

How It Compares

Semaglutide is one of three major players in this space, and where it fits is worth understanding.

Compound Mechanism Trial Weight Loss (approx.)
Semaglutide GLP-1 (single) ~15% (68 weeks)
Tirzepatide GLP-1 + GIP (dual) ~20–22% (higher-dose trials)
Retatrutide GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon (triple) ~24%+ (trials ongoing)

In short: semaglutide is the established, most-studied option with the longest track record; tirzepatide (a dual agonist) has shown somewhat greater average weight loss; and retatrutide (a triple agonist) is the newest, with the highest figures in trials still underway. Semaglutide's strength is its unmatched depth of evidence and real-world experience. For a full side-by-side, see our Retatrutide vs Semaglutide vs Tirzepatide comparison, and our Retatrutide complete guide.

Safety & Who Should Avoid It

Semaglutide has been used by millions of people and studied extensively, with a well-characterized safety profile. Still, it's not for everyone.

Who should not use semaglutide

Semaglutide is contraindicated for anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (a rare thyroid cancer) or a condition called Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 (MEN 2), based on findings in animal studies. It should be avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding, by people with a history of pancreatitis, and used with caution alongside diabetes medications (see below). Anyone with a history of gallbladder disease, severe gastrointestinal conditions, or an eating disorder should consult a doctor first.

The Key Drug Interaction

The most important interaction is with other blood-sugar-lowering medications. Combining semaglutide with insulin or sulfonylureas can push blood sugar too low (hypoglycemia), so those medications often need adjustment by a doctor. Semaglutide's slowing of gastric emptying can also affect the absorption of some oral medications. Our drug interactions guide covers this in detail — this is a genuinely important one to get right if you take other medications.

Common Questions

How much weight can you lose on semaglutide?

In the pivotal STEP 1 trial, people without diabetes lost an average of about 14.9% of their body weight over 68 weeks at the 2.4 mg weekly dose, compared to about 2.4% on placebo. Individual results vary — some lose more, some less — and results depend on dose, consistency, and lifestyle. It's worth noting the trial figure is an average at the full dose reached through proper titration, alongside lifestyle support.

What's the difference between Ozempic and Wegovy?

They're the same molecule — semaglutide — sold under different brand names. Ozempic is branded for type 2 diabetes (up to 2 mg weekly) and is often used off-label for weight, while Wegovy is branded for weight management at a higher 2.4 mg dose. The weight-loss trial results most people cite come from the Wegovy (2.4 mg) dose. Rybelsus is a third brand — a daily oral tablet form used for diabetes.

Why do I have to start at such a low dose?

The 0.25 mg starting dose is entirely about tolerability, not effectiveness — you're not expected to lose much weight at it. Your digestive system needs time to adapt to slowed gastric emptying, and starting too high or escalating too fast is the number-one cause of severe nausea and of people quitting. The slow titration (increasing roughly every 4 weeks) is what lets most people tolerate it well. Patience here genuinely pays off.

Will I regain the weight if I stop?

Research shows much of the weight tends to return after stopping, because semaglutide works by regulating appetite — and that effect ends when the medication does. This is why it's increasingly understood as an ongoing tool for managing a chronic condition (like blood pressure medication) rather than a short-term fix. Building sustainable habits during treatment, and discussing any transition with a doctor, helps — but it's important to go in with realistic expectations.

How do I handle the nausea?

Nausea is the most common side effect, usually worst early and after dose increases, and it typically fades as you adjust. The biggest lever is not rushing the dose titration. Beyond that: eat smaller portions, favor bland lower-fat foods when queasy, avoid greasy or very rich meals, and stay hydrated. If you genuinely can't keep food or water down, that's a reason to contact a healthcare professional rather than push through.

Is semaglutide or tirzepatide better?

Tirzepatide has shown somewhat greater average weight loss in trials (~20–22% vs ~15%), likely because it acts on two receptors (GLP-1 and GIP) rather than one. But semaglutide has the longer track record and deeper body of evidence and real-world experience. "Better" depends on your priorities — proven track record versus higher average results, plus individual tolerance. Our comparison guide covers the trade-offs in detail.

Should I worry about losing muscle?

It's worth being aware of: research suggests roughly 25–40% of weight lost on GLP-1 medications can be lean mass, though this happens with significant weight loss from any cause. The countermeasures are straightforward and effective — eat enough protein (which takes deliberate effort when your appetite is down) and do resistance training. Doing both helps ensure more of what you lose is fat, giving a better body-composition result.

Is semaglutide legal in Costa Rica?

Semaglutide is sold as a research compound in Costa Rica, the same framework used in most countries with active peptide markets, for laboratory and research purposes. Buying locally avoids the heat exposure that international shipping puts delicate peptides through. See our FAQ page for more.

Questions about semaglutide?

Whether you want to understand how semaglutide works, how it compares to other options, or how to approach the titration, reach out. We answer every message personally — no pressure, no upsell.

Contact Us on WhatsApp

Important disclaimer: The information in this guide is general educational content only. It is not medical advice, a prescription, or a personalized recommendation. While semaglutide is an FDA-approved medication under brand names like Ozempic and Wegovy when prescribed by a licensed clinician, research-grade semaglutide is sold as a research compound intended for laboratory and scientific study and is not a substitute for prescribed, medically supervised treatment. Semaglutide is contraindicated in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2, and should be avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before beginning any peptide protocol, especially if you take diabetes medications, have a medical condition, or take other medications. Products sold by Peptides Costa Rica are intended for laboratory and research purposes only.

Metabolismo y peso

Semaglutida: La Guía Completa

El péptido GLP-1 que revolucionó la pérdida de peso, conocido como Ozempic y Wegovy. Aquí te explicamos cómo funciona, qué mostraron realmente los ensayos clínicos y lo que debes saber antes de considerarlo.

Esta guía resume la investigación clínica publicada sobre la semaglutida. Es meramente educativa y no sustituye el consejo de un profesional de la salud calificado. Las fuentes se enumeran al final.

Semaglutida de un vistazo
Clase
Agonista del receptor GLP-1
Nombres de marca
Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus
Prueba de Pérdida de Peso
~15% de peso corporal (68 semanas)
Dosificación
Una vez a la semana, titulada progresivamente
Media vida
~7 días (dosis semanal)

¿Qué hay en esta página?
  1. Qué es la semaglutida
  2. Los nombres explicados
  3. Cómo funciona
  4. Lo que los juicios demostraron
  5. Dosificación y titulación

  7. La Consideración de la Pérdida Muscular
  8. Cómo se compara
  9. Seguridad y Quién Debe Evitarlo
  10. Preguntas frecuentes

Pocos compuestos han cambiado un campo de la manera que la semaglutida cambió el manejo del peso. Cuando se publicaron los datos de su ensayo histórico, demostraron algo que antes se pensaba que solo era posible mediante cirugía: una pérdida de peso sustancial y sostenida a partir de una inyección semanal. Se convirtió en un nombre familiar casi de la noche a la mañana —bajo las marcas Ozempic y Wegovy— y remodeló la forma en que la medicina aborda la obesidad.

Esta guía explica qué es la semaglutida, cómo produce sus efectos, qué demostraron exactamente los ensayos clínicos, cómo se dosifica y las realidades prácticas de los efectos secundarios y consideraciones, todo basado en la investigación publicada.

Qué es la semaglutida

Semaglutida es un Agonista del receptor GLP-1 — un péptido que imita una hormona intestinal natural llamada péptido similar al glucagón 1 (GLP-1). Su cuerpo libera GLP-1 después de comer; ayuda a regular el azúcar en la sangre y señala saciedad. El inconveniente es que el GLP-1 natural se descompone en cuestión de minutos. La semaglutida está diseñada para resistir esa degradación, por lo que una sola inyección sigue actuando durante aproximadamente una semana, razón por la cual se administra solo una vez por semana.

Originalmente se desarrolló para la diabetes tipo 2 (el GLP-1 ayuda a controlar el nivel de azúcar en sangre), pero los investigadores notaron un efecto secundario constante y sorprendente: una pérdida de peso significativa. Esa observación condujo a ensayos dedicados a la obesidad y, en última instancia, a que la semaglutida se convirtiera en el medicamento definitorio para la pérdida de peso de su era.

Los Nombres Explicados (Ozempic vs Wegovy vs Rybelsus)

Una fuente de confusión es que la misma molécula —semaglutida— se vende bajo diferentes nombres comerciales para distintos usos. Aquí está el desglose claro:

Marca Uso principal Formulario
Ozempic Diabetes tipo 2 (uso fuera de indicación para bajar de peso) Inyección semanal, hasta 2 mg
Wegovy Control de peso (obesidad) Inyección semanal, hasta 2.4 mg
Rybelsus Diabetes tipo 2 Tableta oral diaria

Todos son semaglutida; las diferencias son el uso aprobado, la dosis y la forma. Los resultados del ensayo de pérdida de peso que la mayoría cita provienen de la dosis más alta de 2.4 mg (Wegovy). A partir de 2026, también se aprobó una forma de tableta oral de semaglutida para la pérdida de peso, ampliando las opciones más allá de la inyección.

Cómo funciona

La semaglutida produce pérdida de peso a través de varias acciones complementarias: no es un estimulante ni un "quemador de grasa", sino una señal hormonal que cambia cuánto quieres comer.

Reduce el apetito

Actúa sobre los centros del apetito en el cerebro, reduciendo el hambre y los antojos. La mayoría de las personas simplemente se sienten satisfechas con menos comida, el mecanismo central detrás de la pérdida de peso.

Retrasa el vaciamiento gástrico

Retrasa la velocidad a la que el estómago se vacía, por lo que te sientes lleno por más tiempo después de comer. Esta es también la causa de la mayoría de sus efectos secundarios digestivos.

Mejora el control del azúcar en sangre

Estimula la liberación de insulina cuando el nivel de azúcar en la sangre es alto y reduce la producción excesiva de glucosa, el mecanismo original de la diabetes.

Silencia el "ruido de la comida"

Muchos usuarios describen una reducción en pensamientos intrusivos constantes sobre la comida, lo que facilita comer menos sin una fuerza de voluntad a toda costa.

El hallazgo clave

La semaglutida funciona en gran medida mediante reducir el apetito — hace que comer se sienta menos forzado y más natural. Esa reducción del "ruido de la comida" es lo que mucha gente encuentra más sorprendente: el constante impulso de fondo hacia la comida se apaga. Por eso funciona donde las dietas basadas en la fuerza de voluntad a menudo fallan: aborda el impulso biológico de comer, no solo el comportamiento.

Lo que los juicios demostraron

La reputación de la semaglutida se basa en un conjunto inusualmente sólido de evidencia de ensayos clínicos: el programa STEP (Semaglutide Treatment Effect in People with obesity).

El Resultado Histórico

En el crucial ensayo STEP 1 (publicado en la New England Journal of Medicine en 2021), 1.961 adultos con obesidad o sobrepeso — sin diabetes — recibieron semaglutida semanal de 2.4 mg o placebo, junto con apoyo de estilo de vida. Después de 68 semanas, el grupo de semaglutida perdió un promedio de aproximadamente 14,91 TP3T de su peso corporal, en comparación con aproximadamente 2,4% con el placebo. Para un tratamiento no quirúrgico, alcanzar una pérdida de peso promedio cercana a los 15% fue un verdadero punto de inflexión —un nivel que antes se creía que solo se podía lograr mediante cirugía bariátrica—.

Dura

El ensayo STEP 5 amplió el panorama a dos años, mostrando que la pérdida de peso se mantuvo con el tratamiento continuo; este no es solo un efecto a corto plazo que se revierte rápidamente mientras se sigue el tratamiento. A lo largo del programa STEP, los resultados fueron consistentes y, además de la pérdida de peso, la semaglutida también ha demostrado beneficios cardiovasculares en investigaciones separadas.

Una nota sincera sobre cómo detenerse

Un hallazgo importante y bien documentado: gran parte del peso tiende a recuperarse después de suspender la semaglutida, porque el efecto regulador del apetito cesa cuando lo hace la medicación. Esto ha cambiado la forma en que se entiende el compuesto: como una herramienta continua para manejar una condición crónica (similar a los medicamentos para la presión arterial) en lugar de un curso corto que "cura" permanentemente el peso. Vale la pena tener esa comprensión realista desde el principio.

Dosificación y titulación

La dosificación de semaglutida sigue un principio firme: Empieza bajo y aumenta lentamente. Esta titulación gradual es el factor más importante para tolerarlo bien. Los rangos a continuación reflejan el enfoque estándar utilizado en los ensayos y el etiquetado. Son referencias informativas generales, no recomendaciones médicas.

Fase Dosis semanal típica Propósito
Semanas 1–4 0.25 mg Adaptación — no se espera que impulse la pérdida de peso todavía
Semanas 5–8 0.5 mg Adaptación continua
Semanas 9–12 1.0 mg Construyendo hacia una dosis efectiva
Semanas 13 a 16 1.7 miligramos Acercándose al objetivo
Semana 17+ 2.4 mg (objetivo) La dosis completa de control de peso de los ensayos

Por qué no puedes apresurar esto

La dosis inicial de 0.25 mg es aproximadamente tolerabilidad, no efectividad — no deberías esperar una gran pérdida de peso con las dosis más bajas, y eso es por diseño. Saltarse etapas o aumentar la dosis demasiado rápido es la causa más común de náuseas intensas e intolerables y de que las personas abandonen el tratamiento por completo. Tu sistema digestivo necesita tiempo para adaptarse al vaciamiento gástrico más lento. La paciencia durante la titulación es lo que marca la diferencia entre tolerarlo bien y tener una experiencia miserable. Algunas personas también se quedan en una dosis más baja que les funciona en lugar de aumentar siempre a la máxima.

La semaglutida viene como una solución o se reconstituye a partir de polvo con agua bacteriostática, luego se inyectó por vía subcutánea una vez por semana. Ver nuestra reconstitución y conceptos básicos de dosificación guías, y nuestro Guía de almacenamiento tropical para mantenerlo estable con el calor.

Efectos secundarios y cómo manejarlos

Los efectos secundarios de la semaglutida son predecibles y mayormente digestivos, una consecuencia directa de cómo ralentiza el intestino. La buena noticia es que suelen ser más intensos al principio y disminuyen a medida que tu cuerpo se adapta, y hay mucho que puedes hacer para minimizarlos.

Común (usualmente transitorio)

  • Náusea — las más comunes, especialmente al principio y después de aumentar la dosis
  • Estreñimiento o diarrea
  • Apetito reducido (el efecto deseado, pero vale la pena comer suficientes nutrientes)
  • Hinchazón, eructos o reflujo
  • Fatiga, particularmente al principio

Formas prácticas de reducirlos

  • Come porciones más pequeñas; el vaciamiento lento hace que las comidas abundantes se sientan peor.
  • Prefiere alimentos blandos y bajos en grasa cuando sientas náuseas; evita las comidas grasosas y muy pesadas.
  • Mantente hidratado, lo que también ayuda con el estreñimiento
  • No apures el ajuste de la dosis — esta es la palanca más importante
  • Consume suficiente proteína y mantente activo (ver la nota sobre músculos a continuación)

¿Cuándo buscar atención médica?

Comunícate con un profesional de la salud si no puedes retener alimentos o líquidos, o si experimentas dolor abdominal intenso o persistente (especialmente si el dolor se irradia hacia la espalda, lo que puede indicar pancreatitis, una complicación rara pero grave). La pérdida rápida de peso también puede aumentar el riesgo de cálculos biliares. Estos son poco comunes, pero son situaciones en las que la opinión médica es importante. Consulta nuestra cuándo consultar a un médico guía.

La Consideración de la Pérdida Muscular

Un aspecto cada vez más discutido de la pérdida de peso con GLP-1 merece una atención honesta: parte del peso perdido es masa muscular magra, no solo grasa. La investigación sugiere que aproximadamente 25–40% del peso perdido La masa magra puede disminuir al tomar medicamentos GLP-1. Esto no es exclusivo de la semaglutida; una pérdida de peso significativa por cualquier causa implica cierta pérdida muscular, pero vale la pena contrarrestarla activamente.

Cómo proteger tus músculos

Dos contramedidas son las más importantes: come suficiente proteína (esto se vuelve más difícil cuando tu apetito está suprimido, así que necesita ser deliberado) y haz entrenamiento de resistencia (Levantar pesas o trabajar con el peso corporal le indica a tu cuerpo que conserve músculo). Perder peso mientras conservas músculo da como resultado una mejor composición corporal y un mejor resultado metabólico que simplemente ver bajar la báscula. Esto es lo suficientemente importante como para que lo abordemos, y cómo los péptidos de hormona de crecimiento a veces influyen, como parte de una estrategia metabólica más amplia.

Cómo se compara

La semaglutida es uno de los tres actores principales en este ámbito, y vale la pena entender su lugar.

Compuesto Mecanismo Pérdida de peso de prueba (aprox.)
Semaglutida GLP-1 (único) ~15% (68 semanas)
Tirzepatida GLP-1 + GIP (dual) ~20–22% (ensayos con dosis más altas)
Retatrutida GLP-1 + GIP + glucagón (triple) ~24%+ (ensayos en curso)

En resumen: la semaglutida es la opción establecida, más estudiada y con la trayectoria más larga; la tirzepatida (un agonista dual) ha mostrado una pérdida de peso promedio algo mayor; y la retatrutida (un agonista triple) es la más nueva, con las cifras más altas en ensayos aún en curso. La fortaleza de la semaglutida es su profundidad inigualable de evidencia y experiencia en el mundo real. Para una comparación completa lado a lado, consulte nuestra Comparación de Retatrutida, Semaglutida y Tirzepatida, y nuestro Guía completa de retatrutida.

Seguridad y Quién Debe Evitarlo

La semaglutida ha sido utilizada por millones de personas y estudiada extensamente, con un perfil de seguridad bien caracterizado. Aun así, no es para todos.

¿Quiénes no deben usar semaglutida?

La semaglútida es contraindicado para cualquier persona con antecedentes personales o familiares de carcinoma medular de tiroides (un tipo raro de cáncer de tiroides) o de una afección llamada Neoplasia Endocrina Múltiple tipo 2 (NEM 2), basándose en hallazgos de estudios en animales. Debe evitarse en el embarazo y la lactancia, en personas con antecedentes de pancreatitis, y usarse con precaución junto con medicamentos para la diabetes (ver abajo). Cualquier persona con antecedentes de enfermedad de la vesícula biliar, afecciones gastrointestinales graves o un trastorno alimentario debe consultar a un médico primero.

La Interacción Clave de Medicamentos

La interacción más importante es con otros medicamentos hipoglucemiantes. Combinar semaglutida con insulina o sulfonilureas pueden reducir demasiado el nivel de azúcar en sangre (hipoglucemia), por lo que los médicos a menudo necesitan ajustar esas medicaciones. La ralentización del vaciamiento gástrico de la semaglutida también puede afectar la absorción de algunos medicamentos orales. Nuestro guía de interacciones medicamentosas esto lo cubre en detalle — esta es una cuestión realmente importante de abordar correctamente si tomas otros medicamentos.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Cuánta peso se puede perder con semaglutida?

En el ensayo clínico pivotal STEP 1, las personas sin diabetes perdieron un promedio de aproximadamente 14,9% de su peso corporal a lo largo de 68 semanas con la dosis semanal de 2,4 mg, en comparación con aproximadamente 2,4% en el grupo de placebo. Los resultados individuales varían —algunos pierden más, otros menos— y dependen de la dosis, la constancia y el estilo de vida. Vale la pena señalar que la cifra del ensayo es un promedio con la dosis completa, alcanzada mediante una titulación adecuada, junto con apoyo para el estilo de vida.

¿Cuál es la diferencia entre Ozempic y Wegovy?

Son la misma molécula —semaglutida— vendida bajo diferentes nombres comerciales. Ozempic se comercializa para la diabetes tipo 2 (hasta 2 mg semanales) y a menudo se usa fuera de etiqueta para perder peso, mientras que Wegovy se comercializa para el control del peso con una dosis más alta de 2.4 mg. Los resultados de los ensayos de pérdida de peso que la mayoría de la gente cita provienen de la dosis de Wegovy (2.4 mg). Rybelsus es una tercera marca, una tableta oral diaria utilizada para la diabetes.

¿Por qué tengo que empezar con una dosis tan baja?

La dosis inicial de 0.25 mg se enfoca enteramente en la tolerabilidad, no en la efectividad. No se espera que pierdas mucho peso con ella. Tu sistema digestivo necesita tiempo para adaptarse a un vaciamiento gástrico más lento, y comenzar con una dosis demasiado alta o aumentarla demasiado rápido es la causa número uno de náuseas severas y de que las personas abandonen el tratamiento. La titulación lenta (aumento aproximado cada 4 semanas) es lo que permite que la mayoría de las personas la toleren bien. La paciencia aquí realmente vale la pena.

¿Volveré a recuperar el peso si dejo de hacerlo?

Las investigaciones muestran que gran parte del peso tiende a recuperarse después de suspender el tratamiento, porque la semaglutida funciona regulando el apetito, y ese efecto termina cuando el medicamento lo hace. Es por eso que cada vez se entiende más como una herramienta continua para manejar una condición crónica (similar a la medicación para la presión arterial) en lugar de una solución a corto plazo. Construir hábitos sostenibles durante el tratamiento y discutir cualquier transición con un médico ayuda, pero es importante tener expectativas realistas.

¿Cómo manejo las náuseas?

Las náuseas son el efecto secundario más común, generalmente peor al principio y después de aumentos de dosis, y suelen disminuir a medida que te adaptas. La palanca más importante es no apresurar la titulación de la dosis. Más allá de eso: come porciones más pequeñas, prefiere alimentos suaves y bajos en grasa cuando tengas náuseas, evita comidas grasosas o muy pesadas y mantente hidratado. Si realmente no puedes retener comida o agua, esa es una razón para contactar a un profesional de la salud en lugar de seguir adelante.

¿Es mejor la semaglutida o la tirzepatida?

La tirzepatida ha demostrado una pérdida de peso promedio ligeramente mayor en los ensayos (~20–22% frente a ~15%), probablemente porque actúa sobre dos receptores (GLP-1 y GIP) en lugar de uno solo. Sin embargo, la semaglutida cuenta con un historial más extenso, una base de evidencia más sólida y una mayor experiencia en el mundo real. Lo que sea "mejor" depende de tus prioridades: un historial comprobado frente a resultados promedio más altos, además de la tolerancia individual. Nuestra guía comparativa aborda estas ventajas y desventajas en detalle.

¿Debería preocuparme por perder músculo?

Vale la pena tenerlo en cuenta: las investigaciones sugieren que aproximadamente entre el 25 y el 40% del peso perdido con los medicamentos de GLP-1 puede ser masa magra, aunque esto ocurre con cualquier pérdida de peso significativa, independientemente de la causa. Las medidas para contrarrestar esto son sencillas y efectivas: consumir suficiente proteína (lo cual requiere un esfuerzo consciente cuando el apetito está bajo) y realizar entrenamiento de resistencia. Hacer ambas cosas ayuda a garantizar que la mayor parte de lo que se pierde sea grasa, lo que da como resultado una mejor composición corporal.

¿Es legal la semaglutida en Costa Rica?

La semaglutida se vende como compuesto de investigación en Costa Rica, el mismo marco utilizado en la mayoría de los países con mercados activos de péptidos, para fines de laboratorio e investigación. Comprar localmente evita la exposición al calor a la que los péptidos delicados son sometidos durante el envío internacional. Ver nuestro Preguntas frecuentes para más.

¿Preguntas sobre la semaglutida?

Ya sea que quieras entender cómo funciona la semaglutida, cómo se compara con otras opciones o cómo abordar la titulación, contáctanos. Respondemos cada mensaje personalmente, sin presión ni ventas adicionales.

Semax: The Complete Guide

One of the most thoroughly studied nootropic peptides — used in Russian medicine for over three decades. Here's how Semax works, what the research shows, and how it's used.

This guide summarizes published research and clinical history on Semax. It is educational only and not a substitute for advice from a qualified healthcare professional. Sources are listed at the end.

Semax at a Glance
Class
Nootropic / neuroprotective peptide
Structure
ACTH(4–10) analog (heptapeptide)
Best Known For
Focus, drive, memory, neuroprotection
Main Mechanism
BDNF & NGF upregulation
Route
Intranasal (nasal spray/drops)
Regulatory
Used in Russia; not FDA-approved
What's on this page

Most nootropics fall into two camps: stimulants that push your brain harder for a few hours, and supplements whose evidence is so thin you might as well take a sugar pill. Semax is unusual — it sits outside both. Developed by Russian scientists in the 1980s and used in clinical medicine there for over thirty years, it works on the brain's underlying biology rather than simply revving it up, and it has one of the better-documented mechanisms of any nootropic peptide.

This guide covers what Semax is, how its mechanism works, the benefits and honest evidence, dosing and delivery, its variants, and how it compares to its calming cousin Selank. For the wider category, see our pillar guide on nootropic peptides explained.

What Semax Is

Semax is a synthetic peptide of seven amino acids (a heptapeptide), based on a small fragment of a natural hormone called ACTH — specifically the ACTH(4–10) region — with a short "Pro-Gly-Pro" tail added to the end to make it more stable and longer-lasting in the body.

Here's the crucial detail: although it's derived from ACTH (the hormone that normally triggers cortisol release), Semax keeps only the brain-active part and lacks the hormonal portion. That means it acts on the nervous system without triggering any cortisol or stress-hormone response. It's a "clean" neuropeptide — the cognitive effects without the hormonal baggage.

A rare thing: a nootropic with a real clinical history

Semax was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences and has been used in Russian medicine for more than three decades — including an on-label role in stroke recovery. That's a far deeper clinical track record than most compounds in the nootropic space, which is a big part of why Semax is taken seriously by researchers.

How It Works

Semax's central mechanism is well characterized — and it's the heart of why it's considered a genuine nootropic rather than a stimulant.

Raises BDNF & NGF

Its signature action: a rapid, measurable increase in BDNF and NGF (brain growth factors) in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex within hours of a single dose. These drive neuroplasticity, learning, and memory. This is the core pharmacology, not a side effect.

Modulates Dopamine

It increases dopamine turnover in key brain regions, which is consistent with its effects on attention, motivation, drive, and working memory — the "focus and get-things-done" feeling.

Protects Neurons

Semax has neuroprotective effects — reducing damage in low-oxygen (ischemic) conditions by suppressing cell-death pathways and calming inflammation. This underpins its stroke-recovery use.

Not a Classic Stimulant

Importantly, it "nudges" brain-plasticity and stress-response programs rather than forcing the nervous system into overdrive — so it doesn't produce a jittery, caffeine-like buzz.

The through-line: Semax works by supporting the brain's capacity — its ability to form connections, protect its neurons, and stay resilient — with BDNF at the center. One well-known finding is that a single dose changes the expression of hundreds of genes, concentrated in neurotrophin and synaptic-plasticity pathways.

Benefits & Uses

Semax is researched and used for two broad purposes: everyday cognitive enhancement and clinical neuroprotection.

Focus & Attention

Improved concentration and the ability to sustain attention — one of the most commonly reported effects.

Drive & Motivation

A sense of mental energy and motivation to engage with tasks, tied to its dopamine effects.

Memory & Learning

Support for memory consolidation and learning, via BDNF-driven neuroplasticity.

Mental Clarity & Anti-Fatigue

Reduced mental fatigue and clearer thinking, especially under cognitive load.

Neuroprotection

Protection of brain tissue — the basis of its clinical use in stroke recovery in Russia.

Stress Resilience

Support for staying clear-headed and functional under pressure, without raising cortisol.

Effects are clearest "under load"

A useful nuance from the research: Semax's benefits tend to be most measurable when the brain is working hard — during demanding mental tasks, learning, or recovery — rather than as a dramatic everyday "high." If you're expecting a stimulant-like jolt, that's the wrong frame. Think clearer thinking and better performance when you're actually taxing your brain.

The Half-Life Paradox

One of the most interesting things about Semax is a seeming contradiction: it clears from the blood within minutes, yet its effects last for hours to days. How?

The peptide itself is broken down very quickly (the Pro-Gly-Pro tail slows this, but it's still rapid). However, what matters isn't how long the peptide lingers — it's what it triggers. That burst of BDNF and NGF gene activity it sets off in the brain persists long after the peptide is gone, with neurotrophic effects measurable 24 hours or more after a single dose. Subjectively, effects typically begin 20–40 minutes after an intranasal dose, peak around 1–2 hours, and last several hours.

Why this matters for dosing

This paradox is why Semax works despite its ultra-short half-life — you're not dosing to keep the peptide in your system, you're dosing to trigger a longer-lasting biological cascade. It also explains the once- or twice-daily dosing pattern: a brief signal each day is enough to keep the downstream effects going.

Dosing & Delivery

The details below reflect commonly reported protocols and its clinical history. They are a general informational reference, not a medical recommendation, and there is no official dosing guideline since Semax isn't an approved product outside its regions of use.

Aspect Typical Approach
Common dose (standard Semax) 200–600 mcg intranasally, 1–3× daily (often 100–300 mcg for general cognitive use)
Route Intranasal (nasal spray or drops) — the primary route; subcutaneous also used
Timing Earlier in the day (it supports focus/drive; late dosing may affect sleep)
Cycling Often used for stretches of days with breaks, rather than indefinitely
Approach Start at the lower end and adjust; variants are dosed differently (see below)

Why intranasal, not oral

Semax is used intranasally because its oral bioavailability is effectively zero — swallowed, it's destroyed by digestive enzymes before it can work. Intranasal delivery bypasses the gut and even provides some direct "nose-to-brain" transport through the nasal passages, which is why it's the standard route. Don't expect an oral/capsule form to do anything.

For general injection and handling basics, see our dosing basics and, given the climate here, our tropical storage guide (peptides are heat-sensitive).

Semax Variants

You'll encounter a few forms of Semax. They differ mainly in potency and duration, which changes the dose:

Variant What's Different
Standard Semax The original, with the most clinical data behind it
N-Acetyl Semax (NA-Semax) Modified for greater stability and potency — dosed lower (roughly a half to a third)
N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NASA) The most potent/longest-acting, with added dopaminergic emphasis — dosed lowest

The more potent variants are stronger per microgram, so their doses are smaller — a key reason to know exactly which form you have and to verify concentration before setting a protocol.

Side Effects

Semax has a well-documented low adverse-effect profile in the available studies — one of its appeals. The most common issues are related to the nasal route rather than the peptide itself.

  • Mild nasal irritation — the most common, from intranasal use, sometimes with repeated dosing
  • Occasional headache or fatigue, uncommonly
  • Overstimulation if dosed too high — a reason to start low, especially with the potent variants

That said, "well-tolerated in available studies" is not the same as "proven completely safe long-term for everyone" — the long-term safety data in broad populations is limited, as with most research peptides.

Semax vs Selank

Semax and Selank are frequently mentioned together — they came from the same Russian research tradition, share the stabilizing Pro-Gly-Pro tail, and both use the intranasal route. But they do different jobs.

Semax Selank
Primary role Nootropic — focus, drive, neuroprotection Anxiolytic — calm, anti-anxiety
Derived from ACTH(4–10) Tuftsin
Main effect Stimulating/activating (clear focus) Calming (without sedation)
Best when You need drive and mental performance Anxiety or stress is in the way

They're complementary, which is why they're often paired — Semax for daytime focus, Selank for calm. Most data on the combination is preclinical, but the rationale (opposite-but-complementary effects) is sound. For that side, see our peptides for anxiety & stress page.

Safety & Regulatory Status

Semax's decades of Russian clinical use and gentle side-effect profile make it one of the better-characterized nootropic peptides, but a few honest points matter.

What to know before considering it

Semax is not FDA-approved as a drug in the United States — its clinical approval and long track record are in Russia and some neighboring countries. Its regulatory status elsewhere has been actively evolving in 2026. Because it acts on brain chemistry (including dopamine), anyone taking psychiatric or neurological medications, or with a related condition, should consult a healthcare professional before considering it. And significant cognitive difficulties, low mood, or brain-fog that won't lift deserve proper medical evaluation — not self-experimentation. See our when to consult a doctor guide.

Common Questions

What is Semax used for?

Semax is used for cognitive enhancement — focus, drive, motivation, memory, and mental clarity — and for neuroprotection, including an on-label role in stroke recovery in Russian medicine. It works by raising brain growth factors (BDNF and NGF) and modulating dopamine, supporting the brain's plasticity and resilience rather than acting as a stimulant. Its effects are clearest when the brain is under load, during demanding mental tasks.

How does Semax work?

Its core mechanism is a rapid, measurable increase in BDNF and NGF — brain growth factors that drive neuroplasticity, learning, and memory — in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex within hours of a single dose. It also increases dopamine turnover (supporting focus and motivation) and protects neurons against damage. Notably, it derives from ACTH but lacks the hormonal part, so it works on the brain without triggering cortisol.

Does Semax raise cortisol since it comes from ACTH?

No. Although Semax is based on a fragment of ACTH (the hormone that normally stimulates cortisol), it keeps only the brain-active portion and lacks the hormonal part — so it has no corticotropic activity and doesn't raise cortisol. This is exactly what makes it a "clean" neuropeptide: the cognitive and neuroprotective effects without the stress-hormone response.

How is Semax taken?

Almost always intranasally — as a nasal spray or drops — because its oral bioavailability is effectively zero (digestive enzymes destroy it if swallowed). Intranasal delivery bypasses the gut and provides some direct nose-to-brain transport. Subcutaneous injection is also used. It's typically dosed earlier in the day (since it supports focus and drive), often 1–3 times daily, with the exact dose depending on which variant you have.

Why do the effects last if it clears the body in minutes?

This is Semax's "half-life paradox." The peptide itself is broken down within minutes, but that's not the point — what matters is the cascade it triggers. The burst of BDNF and NGF gene activity it sets off in the brain persists long after the peptide is gone, with effects measurable 24 hours or more later. So you dose to trigger a longer-lasting biological process, not to keep the peptide circulating.

What's the difference between Semax and the N-Acetyl variants?

Standard Semax is the original with the most clinical data. N-Acetyl Semax (NA-Semax) is modified for greater stability and potency, so it's dosed lower — roughly a half to a third of standard. N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NASA) is the most potent and longest-acting, with more dopaminergic emphasis, dosed lowest. Because potency differs, it's important to know exactly which form you have and verify concentration before setting a dose.

Is Semax better than Selank?

Neither is "better" — they do different jobs. Semax is primarily a nootropic for focus, drive, and neuroprotection (activating). Selank is primarily an anxiolytic for calm and reduced anxiety (calming), without sedation. Semax suits you when you need mental performance and drive; Selank suits you when anxiety or stress is clouding your thinking. They're complementary and often paired — Semax for daytime focus, Selank for calm.

Is Semax legal in Costa Rica?

Semax is sold as a research compound in Costa Rica, the same framework used in most countries with active peptide markets, for laboratory and research purposes. Buying locally avoids the heat exposure that international shipping puts delicate peptides through. See our FAQ page for more.

Questions about Semax?

Whether you want to understand how it works, which variant fits, or how it compares to Selank, we're happy to help — honestly, including the limits of the evidence. We answer every message personally, with no pressure and no upsell.

Contact Us on WhatsApp

Semax is not approved by the FDA or Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud as a treatment for any condition; it has a clinical history and approval in Russia and some neighboring countries. Research-grade Semax is sold as a research compound intended for laboratory and scientific study, not as a substitute for prescribed, medically supervised treatment. Much supporting evidence is preclinical or from regional clinical use and does not meet the standard of large-scale Western clinical trials, and its melanocortin-receptor profile is not fully settled. Semax acts on brain chemistry, including dopamine — anyone taking psychiatric or neurological medications, or with a related condition, should consult a qualified healthcare professional first, and significant cognitive or mood difficulties deserve professional evaluation. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before beginning any peptide protocol. Products sold by Peptides Costa Rica are intended for laboratory and research purposes only.

Semax was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences and has been used in Russian medicine for more than three decades — including an on-label role in stroke recovery. That's a far deeper clinical track record than most compounds in the nootropic space, which is a big part of why Semax is taken seriously by researchers.

Cómo funciona

Semax's central mechanism is well characterized — and it's the heart of why it's considered a genuine nootropic rather than a stimulant.

Raises BDNF & NGF

Its signature action: a rapid, measurable increase in BDNF and NGF (brain growth factors) in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex within hours of a single dose. These drive neuroplasticity, learning, and memory. This is the core pharmacology, not a side effect.

Modulates Dopamine

It increases dopamine turnover in key brain regions, which is consistent with its effects on attention, motivation, drive, and working memory — the "focus and get-things-done" feeling.

Protects Neurons

Semax has neuroprotective effects — reducing damage in low-oxygen (ischemic) conditions by suppressing cell-death pathways and calming inflammation. This underpins its stroke-recovery use.

Not a Classic Stimulant

Importantly, it "nudges" brain-plasticity and stress-response programs rather than forcing the nervous system into overdrive — so it doesn't produce a jittery, caffeine-like buzz.

The through-line: Semax works by supporting the brain's capacidad — its ability to form connections, protect its neurons, and stay resilient — with BDNF at the center. One well-known finding is that a single dose changes the expression of hundreds of genes, concentrated in neurotrophin and synaptic-plasticity pathways.

Benefits & Uses

Semax is researched and used for two broad purposes: everyday cognitive enhancement and clinical neuroprotection.

Focus & Attention

Improved concentration and the ability to sustain attention — one of the most commonly reported effects.

Drive & Motivation

A sense of mental energy and motivation to engage with tasks, tied to its dopamine effects.

Memory & Learning

Support for memory consolidation and learning, via BDNF-driven neuroplasticity.

Mental Clarity & Anti-Fatigue

Reduced mental fatigue and clearer thinking, especially under cognitive load.

Neuroprotección

Protection of brain tissue — the basis of its clinical use in stroke recovery in Russia.

Resiliencia al estrés

Support for staying clear-headed and functional under pressure, without raising cortisol.

Effects are clearest "under load"

A useful nuance from the research: Semax's benefits tend to be most measurable when the brain is working hard — during demanding mental tasks, learning, or recovery — rather than as a dramatic everyday "high." If you're expecting a stimulant-like jolt, that's the wrong frame. Think clearer thinking and better performance when you're actually taxing your brain.

The Half-Life Paradox

One of the most interesting things about Semax is a seeming contradiction: it clears from the blood within minutes, yet its effects last for hours to days. How?

The peptide itself is broken down very quickly (the Pro-Gly-Pro tail slows this, but it's still rapid). However, what matters isn't how long the peptide lingers — it's what it triggers. That burst of BDNF and NGF gene activity it sets off in the brain persists long after the peptide is gone, with neurotrophic effects measurable 24 hours or more after a single dose. Subjectively, effects typically begin 20–40 minutes after an intranasal dose, peak around 1–2 hours, and last several hours.

Why this matters for dosing

This paradox is why Semax works despite its ultra-short half-life — you're not dosing to keep the peptide in your system, you're dosing to trigger a longer-lasting biological cascade. It also explains the once- or twice-daily dosing pattern: a brief signal each day is enough to keep the downstream effects going.

Dosing & Delivery

The details below reflect commonly reported protocols and its clinical history. They are a general informational reference, not a medical recommendation, and there is no official dosing guideline since Semax isn't an approved product outside its regions of use.

Aspecto Enfoque típico
Common dose (standard Semax) 200–600 mcg intranasally, 1–3× daily (often 100–300 mcg for general cognitive use)
Ruta Intranasal (nasal spray or drops) — the primary route; subcutaneous also used
Momento Earlier in the day (it supports focus/drive; late dosing may affect sleep)
Ciclismo Often used for stretches of days with breaks, rather than indefinitely
Acercamiento Start at the lower end and adjust; variants are dosed differently (see below)

Why intranasal, not oral

Semax is used intranasally because its oral bioavailability is effectively zero — swallowed, it's destroyed by digestive enzymes before it can work. Intranasal delivery bypasses the gut and even provides some direct "nose-to-brain" transport through the nasal passages, which is why it's the standard route. Don't expect an oral/capsule form to do anything.

For general injection and handling basics, see our conceptos básicos de dosificación and, given the climate here, our Guía de almacenamiento tropical (peptides are heat-sensitive).

Semax Variants

You'll encounter a few forms of Semax. They differ mainly in potency and duration, which changes the dose:

Variant What's Different
Standard Semax The original, with the most clinical data behind it
N-Acetil Semax (NA-Semax) Modified for greater stability and potency — dosed lower (roughly a half to a third)
N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NASA) The most potent/longest-acting, with added dopaminergic emphasis — dosed lowest

The more potent variants are stronger per microgram, so their doses are smaller — a key reason to know exactly which form you have and to verify concentration before setting a protocol.

Efectos secundarios

Semax has a well-documented low adverse-effect profile in the available studies — one of its appeals. The most common issues are related to the nasal route rather than the peptide itself.

  • Mild nasal irritation — the most common, from intranasal use, sometimes with repeated dosing
  • Occasional headache or fatigue, incomúnmente
  • Overstimulation if dosed too high — a reason to start low, especially with the potent variants

That said, "well-tolerated in available studies" is not the same as "proven completely safe long-term for everyone" — the long-term safety data in broad populations is limited, as with most research peptides.

Semax vs Selank

Semax and Selank are frequently mentioned together — they came from the same Russian research tradition, share the stabilizing Pro-Gly-Pro tail, and both use the intranasal route. But they do different jobs.

Semax Selank
Primary role Nootropic — focus, drive, neuroprotection Anxiolytic — calm, anti-anxiety
Derivado de ACTH(4–10) Tuftsin
Main effect Stimulating/activating (clear focus) Calming (without sedation)
Best when You need drive and mental performance Anxiety or stress is in the way

They're complementary, which is why they're often paired — Semax for daytime focus, Selank for calm. Most data on the combination is preclinical, but the rationale (opposite-but-complementary effects) is sound. For that side, see our peptides for anxiety & stress page.

Safety & Regulatory Status

Semax's decades of Russian clinical use and gentle side-effect profile make it one of the better-characterized nootropic peptides, but a few honest points matter.

What to know before considering it

Semax is not FDA-approved as a drug in the United States — its clinical approval and long track record are in Russia and some neighboring countries. Its regulatory status elsewhere has been actively evolving in 2026. Because it acts on brain chemistry (including dopamine), anyone taking psychiatric or neurological medications, or with a related condition, should consult a healthcare professional before considering it. And significant cognitive difficulties, low mood, or brain-fog that won't lift deserve proper medical evaluation — not self-experimentation. See our cuándo consultar a un médico guía.

Preguntas frecuentes

What is Semax used for?

Semax is used for cognitive enhancement — focus, drive, motivation, memory, and mental clarity — and for neuroprotection, including an on-label role in stroke recovery in Russian medicine. It works by raising brain growth factors (BDNF and NGF) and modulating dopamine, supporting the brain's plasticity and resilience rather than acting as a stimulant. Its effects are clearest when the brain is under load, during demanding mental tasks.

¿Cómo funciona Semax?

Its core mechanism is a rapid, measurable increase in BDNF and NGF — brain growth factors that drive neuroplasticity, learning, and memory — in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex within hours of a single dose. It also increases dopamine turnover (supporting focus and motivation) and protects neurons against damage. Notably, it derives from ACTH but lacks the hormonal part, so it works on the brain without triggering cortisol.

¿El Semax eleva el cortisol ya que proviene de la ACTH?

No. Although Semax is based on a fragment of ACTH (the hormone that normally stimulates cortisol), it keeps only the brain-active portion and lacks the hormonal part — so it has no corticotropic activity and doesn't raise cortisol. This is exactly what makes it a "clean" neuropeptide: the cognitive and neuroprotective effects without the stress-hormone response.

How is Semax taken?

Almost always intranasally — as a nasal spray or drops — because its oral bioavailability is effectively zero (digestive enzymes destroy it if swallowed). Intranasal delivery bypasses the gut and provides some direct nose-to-brain transport. Subcutaneous injection is also used. It's typically dosed earlier in the day (since it supports focus and drive), often 1–3 times daily, with the exact dose depending on which variant you have.

Why do the effects last if it clears the body in minutes?

This is Semax's "half-life paradox." The peptide itself is broken down within minutes, but that's not the point — what matters is the cascade it triggers. The burst of BDNF and NGF gene activity it sets off in the brain persists long after the peptide is gone, with effects measurable 24 hours or more later. So you dose to trigger a longer-lasting biological process, not to keep the peptide circulating.

What's the difference between Semax and the N-Acetyl variants?

Standard Semax is the original with the most clinical data. N-Acetyl Semax (NA-Semax) is modified for greater stability and potency, so it's dosed lower — roughly a half to a third of standard. N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NASA) is the most potent and longest-acting, with more dopaminergic emphasis, dosed lowest. Because potency differs, it's important to know exactly which form you have and verify concentration before setting a dose.

Is Semax better than Selank?

Neither is "better" — they do different jobs. Semax is primarily a nootropic for focus, drive, and neuroprotection (activating). Selank is primarily an anxiolytic for calm and reduced anxiety (calming), without sedation. Semax suits you when you need mental performance and drive; Selank suits you when anxiety or stress is clouding your thinking. They're complementary and often paired — Semax for daytime focus, Selank for calm.

Is Semax legal in Costa Rica?

Semax is sold as a research compound in Costa Rica, the same framework used in most countries with active peptide markets, for laboratory and research purposes. Buying locally avoids the heat exposure that international shipping puts delicate peptides through. See our Preguntas frecuentes para más.

Questions about Semax?

Whether you want to understand how it works, which variant fits, or how it compares to Selank, we're happy to help — honestly, including the limits of the evidence. We answer every message personally, with no pressure and no upsell.

Contáctenos por WhatsApp

Semax is not approved by the FDA or Costa Rica's Ministerio de Salud as a treatment for any condition; it has a clinical history and approval in Russia and some neighboring countries. Research-grade Semax is sold as a research compound intended for laboratory and scientific study, not as a substitute for prescribed, medically supervised treatment. Much supporting evidence is preclinical or from regional clinical use and does not meet the standard of large-scale Western clinical trials, and its melanocortin-receptor profile is not fully settled. Semax acts on brain chemistry, including dopamine — anyone taking psychiatric or neurological medications, or with a related condition, should consult a qualified healthcare professional first, and significant cognitive or mood difficulties deserve professional evaluation.
